The statue welcomed 14 million immigrants as they arrived via [Ellis Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ellis_Island \"Ellis Island\") by ship in the late 19th and early 20th centuries, and is a symbol of the United States and American ideals of liberty and peace.[[117]](#cite_note-Statue_of_Liberty_UNESCO-120)[[118]](#cite_note-121)\n\nIn 1898, the City of New York was formed with the [consolidation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_of_Greater_New_York \"City of Greater New York\") of Brooklyn (until then a separate city), the County of New York (which then included parts of the Bronx), the County of Richmond, and the western portion of the County of Queens.[[119]](#cite_note-122) The opening of the [New York City Subway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City_Subway \"New York City Subway\") in 1904, first built as separate private systems, helped bind the consolidated city together.[[120]](#cite_note-Cudahy2004-123) In the early 20th century, the city became a world center for industry, commerce, and communication.[[121]](#cite_note-Blake2009-124)\n\nIn 1904, the [steamship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steamship \"Steamship\") *[General Slocum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Slocum \"General Slocum\")* caught fire in the [East River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_River \"East River\"), killing 1,021 people.[[122]](#cite_note-Sheard1998-125) In 1911, the [Triangle Shirtwaist Factory fire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Triangle_Shirtwaist_Factory_fire \"Triangle Shirtwaist Factory fire\"), the city's worst industrial disaster, killed 146 garment workers and spurred the growth of the [International Ladies' Garment Workers' Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Ladies'_Garment_Workers'_Union \"International Ladies' Garment Workers' Union\") and major improvements in building safety standards.[[123]](#cite_note-cornell1-126)\n\n[![A man working on a steel girder high above a city skyline.](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c6/Old_timer_structural_worker2.jpg/250px-Old_timer_structural_worker2.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Old_timer_structural_worker2.jpg)\n\nA [construction worker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Construction_worker \"Construction worker\") atop the [Empire State Building](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Empire_State_Building \"Empire State Building\") during its construction in 1930. The [Chrysler Building](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrysler_Building \"Chrysler Building\") is visible to the right.\n\nNew York's non-White population was 36,620 in 1890.[[107]](#cite_note-Rosenwaike-110): Table 30 New York City was a major destination in the early 20th century for Blacks during the [Great Migration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Migration_(African_American) \"Great Migration (African American)\") from the American South, and by 1916, New York City had the largest urban [African diaspora](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_diaspora \"African diaspora\") in North America.[[124]](#cite_note-GatesHigginbotham2009-127) The [Harlem Renaissance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harlem_Renaissance \"Harlem Renaissance\") of literary and [cultural life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Culture_of_New_York_City \"Culture of New York City\") flourished during the era of [Prohibition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prohibition_in_the_United_States \"Prohibition in the United States\").[[125]](#cite_note-Roche2015-128) The larger economic boom generated the construction of skyscrapers competing in height.[[126]](#cite_note-129)\n\nNew York City became the most populous [urbanized area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urban_area#United_States \"Urban area\") in the world in the early 1920s, overtaking London. The metropolitan area surpassed 10 million in the early 1930s, becoming the first [megacity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Megacity \"Megacity\").[[127]](#cite_note-:1-130) The [Great Depression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Depression \"Great Depression\") saw the election of reformer [Fiorello La Guardia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fiorello_La_Guardia \"Fiorello La Guardia\") as mayor and the fall of Tammany Hall after eighty years of political dominance.[[128]](#cite_note-131)\n\nReturning [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II \"World War II\") veterans created a post-war [economic boom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Business_cycle \"Business cycle\") and the development of large [housing tracts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Housing_tract \"Housing tract\") in eastern Queens and [Nassau County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nassau_County,_New_York \"Nassau County, New York\"), with Wall Street leading America's place as the world's dominant economic power. The [United Nations headquarters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_headquarters \"United Nations headquarters\") was completed in 1952, solidifying New York's global [geopolitical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geopolitical \"Geopolitical\") influence, and the rise of [abstract expressionism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abstract_expressionism \"Abstract expressionism\") in the city precipitated New York's displacement of Paris as the center of the art world.[[129]](#cite_note-132)\n\n### Late 20th and early 21st centuries\n\nMain articles: [History of New York City (1978–present)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_New_York_City_(1978–present) \"History of New York City (1978–present)\") and [September 11 attacks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/September_11_attacks \"September 11 attacks\")\n\n[![A two-story building with brick on the first floor, with two arched doorways, and gray stucco on the second floor, off of which hang numerous rainbow flags.](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/ce/Stonewall_Inn_5_pride_weekend_2016.jpg/250px-Stonewall_Inn_5_pride_weekend_2016.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Stonewall_Inn_5_pride_weekend_2016.jpg)\n\n[Stonewall Inn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stonewall_Inn \"Stonewall Inn\") in [Greenwich Village](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greenwich_Village \"Greenwich Village\"), the site of the June 1969 [Stonewall riots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stonewall_riots \"Stonewall riots\") and the cradle of the modern [LGBTQ+ rights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LGBTQ+_rights \"LGBTQ+ rights\") movement worldwide[[130]](#cite_note-GayGreenwichVillage1-133)[[131]](#cite_note-134)\n\nIn 1969, the [Stonewall riots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stonewall_riots \"Stonewall riots\") were a series of violent protests by members of the [gay community](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gay_community \"Gay community\") against a [police raid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_raid \"Police raid\") that took place in the early morning of June 28, 1969, at the [Stonewall Inn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stonewall_Inn \"Stonewall Inn\") in [Greenwich Village](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greenwich_Village \"Greenwich Village\").[[132]](#cite_note-Murphy2013-135) They are widely considered to be the single most important event leading to the [gay liberation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gay_liberation \"Gay liberation\") movement[[130]](#cite_note-GayGreenwichVillage1-133)[[133]](#cite_note-KentuckyStonewall-136)[[134]](#cite_note-PinkNewsStonewall-137)[[135]](#cite_note-EncycloStonewall-138) and the modern fight for [LGBTQ+ rights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LGBTQ+_rights \"LGBTQ+ rights\").[[136]](#cite_note-NPSStonewall-139)[[137]](#cite_note-ObamaStonewall-140) [Wayne R. Dynes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wayne_R._Dynes \"Wayne R. Dynes\"), author of the *[Encyclopedia of Homosexuality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Encyclopedia_of_Homosexuality \"Encyclopedia of Homosexuality\")*, wrote that [drag queens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drag_queen \"Drag queen\") were the only \"[transgender](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transgender \"Transgender\") folks around\" during the Stonewall riots. The transgender community in New York City played a significant role in fighting for LGBTQ+ equality.[[138]](#cite_note-TransEqualityNYC-141)\n\n[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/7/77/Ford_to_City.PNG/250px-Ford_to_City.PNG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ford_to_City.PNG)\n\nOctober 1975 *[New York Daily News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Daily_News \"New York Daily News\")* front page on President Ford's refusal to help the city avert bankruptcy\n\nIn the 1970s, job losses due to [industrial restructuring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deindustrialization \"Deindustrialization\") caused New York City to suffer from economic problems and rising crime rates.[[139]](#cite_note-142) Growing [fiscal deficits](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_budget_balance \"Government budget balance\") in 1975 led the city to appeal to the federal government for financial aid, which President [Gerald Ford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerald_Ford \"Gerald Ford\") denied in a speech paraphrased by *[New York Daily News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Daily_News \"New York Daily News\")* as \"[FORD TO CITY: DROP DEAD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ford_to_City:_Drop_Dead \"Ford to City: Drop Dead\")\".[[140]](#cite_note-143) The [Municipal Assistance Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Municipal_Assistance_Corporation \"Municipal Assistance Corporation\") was formed and granted oversight authority over the city's finances.[[141]](#cite_note-144) While a resurgence in the financial industry improved the city's economic health in the 1980s, New York's crime rate continued to increase through that decade and into the beginning of the 1990s.[[142]](#cite_note-145)\n\nNew York City's population passed 8 million for the first time in the [2000 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_United_States_census \"2000 United States census\");[[143]](#cite_note-146) further records were set in the [2010](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_United_States_census \"2010 United States census\") and [2020](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census \"2020 United States census\") censuses.[[144]](#cite_note-147) Important new economic sectors, such as [Silicon Alley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silicon_Alley \"Silicon Alley\"), emerged.[[145]](#cite_note-Waller2013-148) The year 2000 was celebrated with fanfare in [Times Square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times_Square \"Times Square\").[[146]](#cite_note-NYC-Y2K-149)\n\n[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e5/North_face_south_tower_after_plane_strike_9-11.jpg/250px-North_face_south_tower_after_plane_strike_9-11.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:North_face_south_tower_after_plane_strike_9-11.jpg)\n\nThe [World Trade Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Trade_Center_(1973–2001) \"World Trade Center (1973–2001)\"), in [Lower Manhattan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lower_Manhattan \"Lower Manhattan\"), during the [September 11 attacks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/September_11_attacks \"September 11 attacks\") in 2001\n\nNew York City suffered the bulk of the [economic damage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economic_effects_of_the_September_11_attacks#New_York_City \"Economic effects of the September 11 attacks\") and the largest loss of human life in the aftermath of the [September 11 attacks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/September_11_attacks \"September 11 attacks\") in 2001.[[147]](#cite_note-Dieterle2017-150) Two of the four hijacked airliners were flown into the Twin Towers of the [World Trade Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Trade_Center_(1973–2001) \"World Trade Center (1973–2001)\"), resulting in the collapse of both buildings and the deaths of 2,753 people, including 343 first responders from the [New York City Fire Department](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City_Fire_Department \"New York City Fire Department\") and 71 law enforcement officers.[[148]](#cite_note-151)\n\n[The area was rebuilt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Trade_Center_site#Planning_for_the_new_World_Trade_Center \"World Trade Center site\") with a [new World Trade Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_World_Trade_Center \"New World Trade Center\"), the [National September 11 Memorial and Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_September_11_Memorial_and_Museum \"National September 11 Memorial and Museum\"), and other new buildings and infrastructure,[[149]](#cite_note-Greenspan2013-152) including the [World Trade Center Transportation Hub](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Trade_Center_Transportation_Hub \"World Trade Center Transportation Hub\"), the city's third-largest hub.[[150]](#cite_note-153) The new One World Trade Center is the tallest skyscraper in the Western Hemisphere[[151]](#cite_note-OneWTCtallest-154) and the [world's seventh-tallest building](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_tallest_buildings_in_the_world \"List of tallest buildings in the world\") by [pinnacle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pinnacle \"Pinnacle\") height, with its [spire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spire \"Spire\") reaching a symbolic 1,776 feet (541.3 m), a reference to the year of [American independence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Declaration_of_Independence \"United States Declaration of Independence\").[[152]](#cite_note-155)[[153]](#cite_note-156)[[154]](#cite_note-157)\n\nThe [Occupy Wall Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Occupy_Wall_Street \"Occupy Wall Street\") protests in [Zuccotti Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zuccotti_Park \"Zuccotti Park\") in the [Financial District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Financial_District,_Manhattan \"Financial District, Manhattan\") of Lower Manhattan began on September 17, 2011, receiving global attention and popularizing the [Occupy movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Occupy_movement \"Occupy movement\") against [social](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_inequality \"Social inequality\") and [economic inequality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economic_inequality \"Economic inequality\") worldwide.[[155]](#cite_note-158)\n\nNew York City was [heavily impacted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Effects_of_Hurricane_Sandy_in_New_York \"Effects of Hurricane Sandy in New York\") by [Hurricane Sandy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Sandy \"Hurricane Sandy\") in October 2012. At least 43 people died in New York City as a result of Sandy, and the economic losses in New York City were estimated at $19 billion.[[156]](#cite_note-159) Flooding led to a days-long shutdown of the subway system,[[157]](#cite_note-160) and the first weather-related closure of the New York Stock Exchange since the [Great Blizzard of 1888](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Blizzard_of_1888 \"Great Blizzard of 1888\").[[158]](#cite_note-161) The resulting long-term damage to multiple subway and road tunnels[[159]](#cite_note-162) spawned long-term efforts towards infrastructural projects to counter [climate change](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Climate_change \"Climate change\") and rising seas, including $15 billion in federal funding received through 2022 towards those resiliency efforts.[[160]](#cite_note-ClimateResiliency2-163)[[161]](#cite_note-164)\n\nIn March 2020, the first case of [COVID-19 in the city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_New_York_City \"COVID-19 pandemic in New York City\") was confirmed.[[162]](#cite_note-165) With its population density and extensive exposure to global travelers, the city rapidly replaced [Wuhan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wuhan \"Wuhan\"), China as the global epicenter of [the pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic \"COVID-19 pandemic\") during the early phase, straining the city's healthcare infrastructure.[[163]](#cite_note-166)[[164]](#cite_note-167) Through March 2023, New York City recorded more than 80,000 deaths from COVID-19-related complications.[[165]](#cite_note-168)\n\n## Geography\n\nMain articles: [Geography of New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geography_of_New_York_City \"Geography of New York City\") and [Geography of New York–New Jersey Harbor Estuary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geography_of_New_York–New_Jersey_Harbor_Estuary \"Geography of New York–New Jersey Harbor Estuary\")\n\n[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d2/Core_of_New_York_City_by_Sentinel-2.jpg/250px-Core_of_New_York_City_by_Sentinel-2.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Core_of_New_York_City_by_Sentinel-2.jpg)\n\nAerial view of the [New York City metropolitan area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_metropolitan_area \"New York metropolitan area\") with Manhattan at its center\n\nNew York City lies in the northeastern United States, in southeastern New York State, approximately halfway between Washington, D.C. and [Boston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston \"Boston\"). Its location at the mouth of the [Hudson River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hudson_River \"Hudson River\"), which feeds into a naturally sheltered harbor and then into the Atlantic Ocean, has helped the city become a significant trading port. Most of the city is built on the three islands of [Long Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long_Island \"Long Island\"), [Manhattan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manhattan \"Manhattan\"), and [Staten Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Staten_Island \"Staten Island\").\n\nDuring the [Wisconsin glaciation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wisconsin_glaciation \"Wisconsin glaciation\"), 75,000 to 11,000 years ago, the New York City area was situated at the edge of a large [ice sheet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ice_sheet \"Ice sheet\").[[166]](#cite_note-JacksonKeller2010a-169) The erosive forward movement of the ice (and its subsequent retreat) contributed to the separation of what is now Long Island and Staten Island. That action left [bedrock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bedrock \"Bedrock\") at a relatively shallow depth, providing a solid [foundation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foundation_(engineering) \"Foundation (engineering)\") for most of Manhattan's skyscrapers.[[167]](#cite_note-170)\n\nThe Hudson River flows through the Hudson Valley into [New York Bay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Bay \"New York Bay\"). Between New York City and [Troy, New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Troy,_New_York \"Troy, New York\"), the river is an [estuary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estuary \"Estuary\").[[168]](#cite_note-171) The Hudson River separates the city from New Jersey. The East River—a [tidal strait](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tidal_strait \"Tidal strait\")—flows from [Long Island Sound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long_Island_Sound \"Long Island Sound\") and separates the Bronx and Manhattan from Long Island. The [Harlem River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harlem_River \"Harlem River\"), another tidal strait between the East and Hudson rivers, separates most of Manhattan from the Bronx. The [Bronx River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bronx_River \"Bronx River\"), which flows through the Bronx and [Westchester County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Westchester_County \"Westchester County\"), is the only entirely [freshwater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freshwater \"Freshwater\") river in the city.[[169]](#cite_note-nytimes-172)[*[importance?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:What_Wikipedia_is_not#Encyclopedic_content \"Wikipedia:What Wikipedia is not\")*]\n\nThe city's land has been altered substantially by human intervention, with considerable [land reclamation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Land_reclamation \"Land reclamation\") along the [waterfronts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waterfront_(area) \"Waterfront (area)\") since Dutch colonial times; reclamation is most prominent in Lower Manhattan, with developments such as [Battery Park City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battery_Park_City \"Battery Park City\") in the 1970s and 1980s.[[170]](#cite_note-gillespie-p71-173) Some of the natural relief in topography has been evened out, especially in Manhattan.[[171]](#cite_note-174)\n\nThe city's total area is 468.484 square miles (1,213.37 km2). 302.643 sq mi (783.84 km2) of the city is land and 165.841 sq mi (429.53 km2) of it is water.[[172]](#cite_note-CensusGazetteer-175)[[173]](#cite_note-NYT_Land_Estimate-176) The highest point in the city is [Todt Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Todt_Hill \"Todt Hill\") on Staten Island, which, at 409.8 feet (124.9 m) [above sea level](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Above_sea_level \"Above sea level\"), is the highest point on the eastern seaboard south of [Maine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maine \"Maine\").[[174]](#cite_note-177) The summit of the ridge is mostly covered in [woodlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woodland \"Woodland\") as part of the [Staten Island Greenbelt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Staten_Island_Greenbelt \"Staten Island Greenbelt\").[[175]](#cite_note-178)\n\n### Boroughs\n\nMain articles: [Boroughs of New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boroughs_of_New_York_City \"Boroughs of New York City\") and [Neighborhoods in New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neighborhoods_in_New_York_City \"Neighborhoods in New York City\")\n\n[![A map showing five boroughs in different colors.](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/34/5_Boroughs_Labels_New_York_City_Map.svg/250px-5_Boroughs_Labels_New_York_City_Map.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:5_Boroughs_Labels_New_York_City_Map.svg)\n\n1. [Manhattan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manhattan \"Manhattan\") (New York County)\n\n2. [Brooklyn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brooklyn \"Brooklyn\") (Kings County)\n\n3. [Queens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queens \"Queens\") (Queens County)\n\n4. [The Bronx](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bronx \"The Bronx\") (Bronx County)\n\n5. [Staten Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Staten_Island \"Staten Island\") (Richmond County)\n\nNew York City is sometimes referred to collectively as the *Five Boroughs*.[[176]](#cite_note-179) Each borough is coextensive with a respective [county](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Administrative_divisions_of_New_York_(state)#County \"Administrative divisions of New York (state)\") of New York State, making New York City one of the [U.S. municipalities in multiple counties](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_U.S._municipalities_in_multiple_counties \"List of U.S. municipalities in multiple counties\").\n\n[Manhattan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manhattan \"Manhattan\") (New York County) is the geographically smallest and most densely populated borough. It is home to Central Park and most of the city's skyscrapers, and is sometimes known regionally as *The City*.[[177]](#cite_note-ManhattanTheCity-180) Manhattan's population density of 70,450.8 inhabitants per square mile (27,201.2/km2) in 2022 makes it the [highest of any county in the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_statistics_of_the_United_States#Population_density \"County statistics of the United States\") and [higher than the density of any individual American city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_United_States_cities_by_population_density#New_York_City_boroughs \"List of United States cities by population density\").[[178]](#cite_note-CensusDensity2022-181) Manhattan is the cultural, administrative, and [financial center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Financial_center \"Financial center\") of New York City and contains the headquarters of many major [multinational corporations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multinational_corporation \"Multinational corporation\"), the [United Nations headquarters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_headquarters \"United Nations headquarters\"), Wall Street, and many important universities. The borough is often described as the financial and cultural center of the world.[[179]](#cite_note-182)[[180]](#cite_note-183)\n\n[Brooklyn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brooklyn \"Brooklyn\") (Kings County), on the western tip of [Long Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long_Island \"Long Island\"), is the city's most populous borough. Brooklyn is known for its cultural, social, and ethnic diversity, an independent music and art scene, [distinct neighborhoods](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Brooklyn_neighborhoods \"List of Brooklyn neighborhoods\"), and a distinctive architectural heritage. [Downtown Brooklyn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Downtown_Brooklyn \"Downtown Brooklyn\") is the largest central core neighborhood in the Outer Boroughs. The borough has a long beachfront shoreline including [Coney Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coney_Island \"Coney Island\"), established in the 1870s as one of the earliest amusement grounds in the United States[[181]](#cite_note-184) [Marine Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marine_Park_(Brooklyn_park) \"Marine Park (Brooklyn park)\") and [Prospect Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prospect_Park_(Brooklyn) \"Prospect Park (Brooklyn)\") are the two largest parks in Brooklyn.[[182]](#cite_note-185) Since 2010, Brooklyn has evolved into a hub of [entrepreneurship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Entrepreneurship \"Entrepreneurship\") and [high technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High_tech \"High tech\") [startup firms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Startup_company \"Startup company\"),[[183]](#cite_note-BrooklynDesignHub-186) and of [postmodern art](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Postmodern_art \"Postmodern art\") and design.[[183]](#cite_note-BrooklynDesignHub-186)[[184]](#cite_note-BrooklynArt1-187) Brooklyn is also home to [Fort Hamilton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Hamilton \"Fort Hamilton\"), the [U.S. military's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Armed_Forces \"United States Armed Forces\") only active duty installation within New York City,[[185]](#cite_note-188) aside from [Coast Guard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Coast_Guard \"U.S. Coast Guard\") operations. The facility was established in 1825 on the site of a [battery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artillery_battery \"Artillery battery\") used during the [American Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Revolution \"American Revolution\"), and it is one of America's longest-serving military forts.[[186]](#cite_note-189)\n\n[Queens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queens \"Queens\") (Queens County), on Long Island north and east of Brooklyn, is geographically the largest borough, the most [ethnically diverse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethnically_diverse \"Ethnically diverse\") county in the United States,[[187]](#cite_note-queensdiverse-190) and the most ethnically diverse urban area in the world.[[188]](#cite_note-QueensMostDiverseWorld1-191)[[189]](#cite_note-QueensMostDiverseWorld2-192) Queens is the site of the [Citi Field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citi_Field \"Citi Field\"), home of the [New York Mets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Mets \"New York Mets\"), and hosts the annual [US Open tennis tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/US_Open_(tennis) \"US Open (tennis)\") at the [USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USTA_Billie_Jean_King_National_Tennis_Center \"USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center\") in [Flushing Meadows–Corona Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flushing_Meadows–Corona_Park \"Flushing Meadows–Corona Park\"), with plans to build [Etihad Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Etihad_Park \"Etihad Park\"), a soccer-specific stadium for [New York City FC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City_FC \"New York City FC\").[[190]](#cite_note-193) Additionally, two of the three busiest airports serving the New York metropolitan area, [John F. Kennedy International Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_International_Airport \"John F. Kennedy International Airport\") and [LaGuardia Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LaGuardia_Airport \"LaGuardia Airport\"), are in Queens.[[191]](#cite_note-194)\n\n[The Bronx](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bronx \"The Bronx\") (Bronx County) is both New York City's northernmost borough and the only one that is mostly on the [U.S. mainland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._mainland \"U.S. mainland\"). It is the location of [Yankee Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yankee_Stadium \"Yankee Stadium\"), the baseball park of the [New York Yankees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Yankees \"New York Yankees\"), and home to the largest [cooperatively-owned housing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Housing_cooperative \"Housing cooperative\") complex in the United States, [Co-op City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Co-op_City \"Co-op City\").[[192]](#cite_note-195) It is home to the [Bronx Zoo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bronx_Zoo \"Bronx Zoo\"), the world's largest metropolitan zoo,[[193]](#cite_note-BronxZoo-196) which spans 265 acres (1.07 km2) and houses more than 6,000 animals.[[194]](#cite_note-197) The Bronx is the birthplace of [hip-hop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hip-hop \"Hip-hop\") and its associated [culture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hip_hop_culture \"Hip hop culture\").[[195]](#cite_note-Toop-1992-198) [Pelham Bay Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pelham_Bay_Park \"Pelham Bay Park\") is the largest park in New York City, at 2,772 acres (1,122 ha).[[196]](#cite_note-nyt20130601-199)\n\n[Staten Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Staten_Island \"Staten Island\") (Richmond County) is the most suburban in character of the five boroughs. It is connected to Brooklyn by the [Verrazzano–Narrows Bridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Verrazzano–Narrows_Bridge \"Verrazzano–Narrows Bridge\"), and to Manhattan by way of the free [Staten Island Ferry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Staten_Island_Ferry \"Staten Island Ferry\"). Staten Island is known as the \"Borough of Parks\"[[197]](#cite_note-200) and \"the Greenest Borough\" due to its 12,300 acres of protected parkland and over 170 parks.[[198]](#cite_note-:0-201) In central Staten Island, the [Staten Island Greenbelt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Staten_Island_Greenbelt \"Staten Island Greenbelt\") spans approximately 2,500 acres (10 km2), including 28 miles (45 km) of walking trails and one of the last undisturbed forests in the city.[[199]](#cite_note-202) Designated in 1984 to protect the island's natural lands, the Greenbelt comprises seven city parks. It also contains environmental centers for educational and recreational purposes.[[198]](#cite_note-:0-201)\n\n### Climate\n\nMain article: [Climate of New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Climate_of_New_York_City \"Climate of New York City\")\n\n| New York |\n| --- |\n| Climate chart ([explanation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Template:Climate_chart/How_to_read_a_climate_chart \"Template:Climate chart/How to read a climate chart\")) |\n| |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | J | F | M | A | M | J | J | A | S | O | N | D | | 3.6      40  28 | 3.2      42  30 | 4.3      50  36 | 4.1      62  46 | 4      71  55 | 4.5      80  64 | 4.6      85  70 | 4.6      83  69 | 4.3      76  62 | 4.4      65  51 | 3.6      54  42 | 4.4      44  34 | | █ Average max. and min. temperatures in °F | | █ Precipitation totals in inches | | Source: \"New York City Weatherbox NOAA\" | |\n| | Metric conversion | | --- | | J | F | M | A | M | J | J | A | S | O | N | D | | 92      4  −2 | 81      6  −1 | 109      10  2 | 104      17  8 | 101      22  13 | 115      27  18 | 117      29  21 | 116      29  21 | 109      25  17 | 111      18  11 | 91      12  6 | 111      7  1 | | █ Average max. and min. temperatures in °C | | █ Precipitation totals in mm | |\n\nUnder the [Köppen climate classification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Köppen_climate_classification \"Köppen climate classification\"), New York City has a [humid subtropical climate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humid_subtropical_climate \"Humid subtropical climate\") (*Cfa*) and is the northernmost major city on the North American continent with this categorization. The suburbs to the immediate north and west are in the transitional zone between humid subtropical and [humid continental climates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humid_continental_climate \"Humid continental climate\") (*Dfa*).[[200]](#cite_note-Peel,_M._C.;_Finlayson,_B._L.;_McMahon,_T._A-203)[[201]](#cite_note-newyorkpolonia.com-204) The city receives an average of 49.5 inches (1,260 mm) of precipitation annually, which is relatively evenly spread throughout the year. New York averages [over 2,500 hours of sunshine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Climate_of_New_York_City#Other_phenomena \"Climate of New York City\") annually.[[202]](#cite_note-NYCSunshine-205)\n\nWinters are chilly and damp, and prevailing wind patterns that blow [sea breezes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_breeze \"Sea breeze\") offshore temper the moderating effects of the [Atlantic Ocean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_Ocean \"Atlantic Ocean\"). The Atlantic and the partial shielding from colder air by the [Appalachian Mountains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Appalachian_Mountains \"Appalachian Mountains\") keep the city warmer in the winter than inland North American cities at similar or even lower latitudes.[[203]](#cite_note-206) The daily mean temperature in January, the area's coldest month, is 33.3 °F (0.7 °C).[[204]](#cite_note-NOAA_txt-207) Temperatures usually drop to 10 °F (−12 °C) several times per winter,[[205]](#cite_note-NYC_climate-208) and can reach 60 °F (16 °C) for several days even in the coldest winter month. Spring and autumn are unpredictable and can range from cool to warm, although they are usually mild with low humidity. Summers are typically hot and humid, with a daily mean temperature of 77.5 °F (25.3 °C) in July.[[204]](#cite_note-NOAA_txt-207)\n\nNighttime temperatures are 9.5 °F (5.3 °C) degrees higher for the average city resident due to the [urban heat island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urban_heat_island \"Urban heat island\") effect, caused by paved streets and tall buildings.[[206]](#cite_note-209) Daytime temperatures exceed 90 °F (32 °C) on average of 17 days each summer and in some years exceed 100 °F (38 °C), although this is rare;[[207]](#cite_note-New_York_City_Weatherbox_NOAA-210)[[208]](#cite_note-New_York_City_Weatherbox_NOAA_txt-211)[[209]](#cite_note-noaasun-212)[[210]](#cite_note-Weather_Atlas_NYC-213) the most recent occurrence was measured at [Belvedere Castle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belvedere_Castle \"Belvedere Castle\") in [Central Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Park \"Central Park\") on July 2, 2026, which was the first time since 2012.[[211]](#cite_note-214) Readings of 0 °F (−18 °C) are extremely rare, last occurring on February 14, 2016.[[212]](#cite_note-215)\n\nExtreme temperatures have ranged from 106 °F (41 °C), recorded on July 9, 1936, down to −15 °F (−26 °C) on February 9, 1934.[[204]](#cite_note-NOAA_txt-207) The coldest recorded wind chill was −37 °F (−38 °C) on the same day as the all-time record low.[[213]](#cite_note-216) The average winter snowfall between 1991 and 2020 was 29.8 inches (76 cm). This varies considerably between years. The record cold daily maximum was 2 °F (−17 °C) on December 30, 1917. The record warm daily minimum was 87 °F (31 °C), on July 2, 1903.[[207]](#cite_note-New_York_City_Weatherbox_NOAA-210) The average water temperature of the nearby Atlantic Ocean ranges from 39.7 °F (4.3 °C) in February, to 74.1 °F (23.4 °C) in August.[[214]](#cite_note-217) The New York metropolitan area's coastline constitutes one of the [fastest-warming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Global_warming \"Global warming\") urban ocean [shorelines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coast \"Coast\") in the world.[[215]](#cite_note-NYCFastestWarmingUrbanShorelineWorld-218)\n\n[Hurricanes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane \"Hurricane\") and [tropical storms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_storm \"Tropical storm\") are rare in the New York area.[[216]](#cite_note-219) Hurricane Sandy brought a destructive [storm surge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Storm_surge \"Storm surge\") to New York City on the evening of October 29, 2012, flooding numerous streets, tunnels, and subway lines in Lower Manhattan and other areas of the city and cutting off electricity in many parts of the city and its suburbs.[[217]](#cite_note-220) The storm and its profound impacts have prompted the discussion of constructing [seawalls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seawall \"Seawall\") and other coastal barriers around the shorelines of the city and the metropolitan area to minimize the risk of destructive consequences from another such event in the future.[[160]](#cite_note-ClimateResiliency2-163)\n\n| * [v](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Template:New_York_City_weatherbox \"Template:New York City weatherbox\") * Manhattan\") as seen from [Gapstow Bridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gapstow_Bridge \"Gapstow Bridge\") in [Central Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Park \"Central Park\")\n\nThe city of New York has a complex park system, with various lands operated by the [National Park Service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Park_Service \"National Park Service\"), the [New York State and Historic Preservation\"), and the [New York City Department of Parks and Recreation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City_Department_of_Parks_and_Recreation \"New York City Department of Parks and Recreation\"). In its 2023 ParkScore ranking, the [Trust for Public Land](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trust_for_Public_Land \"Trust for Public Land\") reported that the park system in New York City was the tenth-best park system among the most populous U.S. cities, citing the city's park acreage, investment in parks, and that 99% of residents are within 1⁄2 mile (0.80 km) of a park.[[224]](#cite_note-230)\n\n[Gateway National Recreation Area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gateway_National_Recreation_Area \"Gateway National Recreation Area\") contains over 26,000 acres (110 km2), most of it in New York City.[[225]](#cite_note-231) In Brooklyn and Queens, the park contains over 9,000 acres (36 km2) of [salt marsh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salt_marsh \"Salt marsh\"), [wetlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wetland \"Wetland\"), islands, and water, including most of [Jamaica Bay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamaica_Bay \"Jamaica Bay\") and the [Jamaica Bay Wildlife Refuge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamaica_Bay_Wildlife_Refuge \"Jamaica Bay Wildlife Refuge\"). Also in Queens, the park includes a significant portion of the western [Rockaway Peninsula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rockaway_Peninsula \"Rockaway Peninsula\"), most notably [Jacob Riis Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacob_Riis_Park \"Jacob Riis Park\") and [Fort Tilden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Tilden \"Fort Tilden\").[[226]](#cite_note-232) In Staten Island, it includes [Fort Wadsworth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Wadsworth \"Fort Wadsworth\"), with historic pre-Civil War era [Battery Weed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battery_Weed \"Battery Weed\") and [Fort Tompkins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Tompkins_Quadrangle \"Fort Tompkins Quadrangle\"), and [Great Kills Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Kills_Park \"Great Kills Park\").[[227]](#cite_note-233)\n\nThe [Statue of Liberty National Monument](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Liberty_National_Monument \"Statue of Liberty National Monument\") and [Ellis Island Immigration Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ellis_Island_Immigration_Museum \"Ellis Island Immigration Museum\") are managed by the National Park Service and are in both New York and New Jersey. They are joined in the harbor by [Governors Island National Monument](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governors_Island_National_Monument \"Governors Island National Monument\"). Historic sites under federal management on Manhattan Island include [Stonewall National Monument](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stonewall_National_Monument \"Stonewall National Monument\"); [Castle Clinton National Monument](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Castle_Clinton_National_Monument \"Castle Clinton National Monument\"); Federal Hall National Memorial; [Theodore Roosevelt Birthplace National Historic Site](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theodore_Roosevelt_Birthplace_National_Historic_Site \"Theodore Roosevelt Birthplace National Historic Site\"); [General Grant National Memorial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Grant_National_Memorial \"General Grant National Memorial\") (Grant's Tomb); [African Burial Ground National Monument](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Burial_Ground_National_Monument \"African Burial Ground National Monument\"); and [Hamilton Grange National Memorial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamilton_Grange_National_Memorial \"Hamilton Grange National Memorial\"). [Hundreds of properties](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_National_Historic_Landmarks_in_New_York_City \"List of National Historic Landmarks in New York City\") are listed on the [National Register of Historic Places](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Register_of_Historic_Places \"National Register of Historic Places\") or as a [National Historic Landmark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Historic_Landmark \"National Historic Landmark\").\n\nThere are seven state parks within New York City. They include: the [Clay Pit Ponds State Park Preserve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clay_Pit_Ponds_State_Park_Preserve \"Clay Pit Ponds State Park Preserve\"), a natural area that includes extensive [riding trails](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trail_riding \"Trail riding\"); the [Riverbank State Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverbank_State_Park \"Riverbank State Park\"), a 28-acre (11 ha) facility;[[228]](#cite_note-234) and the [Marsha P. Johnson State Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marsha_P._Johnson_State_Park \"Marsha P. Johnson State Park\"), a state park in Brooklyn and Manhattan that borders the East River renamed in honor of [Marsha P. Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marsha_P._Johnson \"Marsha P. Johnson\").[[229]](#cite_note-235)\n\nNew York City has over 28,000 acres (110 km2) of [municipal parkland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urban_park \"Urban park\") and 14 miles (23 km) of public beaches.[[230]](#cite_note-236) The largest municipal park in the city is Pelham Bay Park in the Bronx, with 2,772 acres (1,122 ha),[[196]](#cite_note-nyt20130601-199)[[231]](#cite_note-237) and the most visited urban park is the [Central Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Park \"Central Park\"), and one of the most filmed and visited locations in the world, with 42 million visitors in 2023.[[232]](#cite_note-NYCvisitors-238)\n\n### Environment\n\nMain article: [Environmental issues in New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Environmental_issues_in_New_York_City \"Environmental issues in New York City\")\n\n[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f7/Recycling_combine_-_Sunset_Pk%2C_NYC_05.jpg/250px-Recycling_combine_-_Sunset_Pk%2C_NYC_05.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Recycling_combine_-_Sunset_Pk,_NYC_05.jpg)\n\nThe [Sunset Park Material Recovery Facility](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunset_Park_Material_Recovery_Facility \"Sunset Park Material Recovery Facility\") is the largest [commingled recycling facility](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Single-stream_recycling \"Single-stream recycling\") in the United States.[[233]](#cite_note-239)[[234]](#cite_note-240)\n\nEnvironmental issues in New York City are affected by the city's size, density, [abundant public transportation infrastructure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transportation_in_New_York_City \"Transportation in New York City\"), and its location at the mouth of the Hudson River. For example, it is one of the country's biggest sources of pollution and has the lowest per-capita [greenhouse gas emissions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greenhouse_gas_emissions \"Greenhouse gas emissions\") rate and electricity usage. [Governors Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governors_Island \"Governors Island\") is planned to host a US$1 billion research and education center to make New York City the global leader in addressing the [climate crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Climate_change \"Climate change\").[[235]](#cite_note-NYCGlobalClimateLeader-241)\n\nAs an [oceanic port](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port \"Port\") city, New York City is vulnerable to long-term manifestations of [global warming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Global_warming \"Global warming\") like [sea level rise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_level_rise \"Sea level rise\") exacerbated by [land subsidence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Land_subsidence \"Land subsidence\").[[236]](#cite_note-242) Climate change has spawned the development of a significant [climate resiliency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_economy \"Green economy\") and [environmental sustainability](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Environmental_sustainability \"Environmental sustainability\") economy in the city. New York City has focused on reducing its [environmental impact](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_impact_on_the_environment \"Human impact on the environment\") and [carbon footprint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carbon_footprint \"Carbon footprint\").[[237]](#cite_note-NYCCarbonFootprint-243) [Mass transit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mass_transit \"Mass transit\") use is the highest in the country.\n\nNew York's [high rate of public transit use](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_U.S._cities_with_high_transit_ridership \"List of U.S. cities with high transit ridership\"), more than 610,000 daily cycling trips as of 2022[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=New_York_City&action=edit),[[238]](#cite_note-NYCcycling-244) and [many pedestrian commuters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_U.S._cities_with_most_pedestrian_commuters \"List of U.S. cities with most pedestrian commuters\") make it the most energy-efficient major city in the United States.[[239]](#cite_note-NYC_energy_consumption-245) Walk and bicycle modes of travel account for 21% of all modes for trips in the city; nationally, the rate for metro regions is about 8%.[[240]](#cite_note-246) In both 2011 and 2015, [Walk Score](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walk_Score \"Walk Score\") named New York City the most [walkable](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walkable \"Walkable\") large city in the United States,[[241]](#cite_note-247)[[242]](#cite_note-248)[[243]](#cite_note-249) and in 2018, *Stacker* ranked New York the most walkable American city.[[244]](#cite_note-250) [Citibank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citibank \"Citibank\") sponsored public bicycles for the city's [bike-share](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bike-share \"Bike-share\") project, which became known as [Citi Bike](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citi_Bike \"Citi Bike\"), in 2013.[[245]](#cite_note-251) New York City's numerical \"in-season cycling indicator\" of bicycling in the city had hit an all-time high of 437 when measured in 2014.[[246]](#cite_note-252)\n\nThe New York City drinking water supply is extracted from the protected [Catskill Mountains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catskill_Mountains \"Catskill Mountains\") watershed.[[247]](#cite_note-253) As a result of the watershed's integrity and undisturbed natural [water filtration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Water_filtration \"Water filtration\") system, New York is one of only four major cities in the United States the majority of whose drinking water is pure enough not to require [water treatment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Water_treatment \"Water treatment\").[[248]](#cite_note-254) The city's municipal water system is the nation's largest, moving more than 1 billion U.S. gallons (3.8 billion liters) of water daily from a watershed covering 1,900 square miles (4,900 km2)[[249]](#cite_note-NYTimes-Water-Investment-2018-255)[[250]](#cite_note-256)\n\nAccording to the 2016 [World Health Organization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Health_Organization \"World Health Organization\") Global Urban Ambient Air Pollution Database,[[251]](#cite_note-257) the annual average concentration in New York City's air of particulate matter measuring 2.5 micrometers or less (PM2.5) was 7.0 micrograms per cubic meter, or 3.0 micrograms within the recommended limit of the WHO Air Quality Guidelines for the annual mean [PM2.5](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PM2.5 \"PM2.5\").[[252]](#cite_note-258) The [New York City Department of Health and Mental Hygiene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City_Department_of_Health_and_Mental_Hygiene \"New York City Department of Health and Mental Hygiene\"), in partnership with [Queens College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queens_College \"Queens College\"), conducts the New York Community Air Survey to measure pollutants at about 150 locations.[[253]](#cite_note-259)\n\n## [[g]](#cite_note-262) |\n\nNew York City is the most populous city in the United States, with 8,804,190 residents as of the [2020 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census \"2020 United States census\"), its highest decennial count ever, incorporating more immigration into the city than outmigration since the [2010 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_United_States_census \"2010 United States census\").[[256]](#cite_note-QuickFacts-263)[[257]](#cite_note-264)[[258]](#cite_note-nytimes_a-265) More than twice as many people live in New York City as in Los Angeles, the second largest American city.[[259]](#cite_note-estimate2023a-266) The city's population in 2020 was 35.9% [White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Americans \"White Americans\"), 22.7% [Black](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Americans \"African Americans\"), 14.6% [Asian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asian_Americans \"Asian Americans\"), 10.5% [Mixed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multiracial_Americans \"Multiracial Americans\"), 0.7% Native American and 0.1% [Pacific Islander](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Islander_Americans \"Pacific Islander Americans\"); 28.4% identified themselves as [Hispanic or Latino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hispanic_and_Latino_Americans \"Hispanic and Latino Americans\").[[256]](#cite_note-QuickFacts-263)\n\nBetween 2010 and 2020, New York City's population grew by 629,000 residents, more than the total growth of the next four largest American cities (Los Angeles, Chicago, [Houston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston \"Houston\"), and [Phoenix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phoenix,_Arizona \"Phoenix, Arizona\")) combined.[[260]](#cite_note-2010to2020CensusGrowth1-267)[[261]](#cite_note-2010to2020CensusGrowth2-268) The city's population density of 27,744.1 inhabitants per square mile (10,712.1/km2) makes it the densest of any American municipality with a population above 100,000.[[178]](#cite_note-CensusDensity2022-181) Manhattan's population density is 70,450.8 inhabitants per square mile (27,201.2/km2), the [highest of any county in the United States.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_statistics_of_the_United_States \"County statistics of the United States\")[[178]](#cite_note-CensusDensity2022-181)\n\nBased on data from the 2020 census, New York City comprised about 43.6% of the state's population of 20,202,320,[[256]](#cite_note-QuickFacts-263) and about 39% of the population of the [New York metropolitan area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_metropolitan_area \"New York metropolitan area\").[[262]](#cite_note-PopHousingEstMetro-269) The majority of New York City residents in 2020 (5,141,539 or 58.4%) were living in Brooklyn or Queens, the two boroughs on Long Island.[[263]](#cite_note-QuickFactsFiveBoroughs-270) An estimated 800 languages are spoken in New York,[[25]](#cite_note-NYCWorld'sMostCulturallyLinguisticallyDiverseCityTop-28)[[27]](#cite_note-QueensMostLinguisticallyDiverseTop-30)[[264]](#cite_note-271)[[265]](#cite_note-800source3-272) and the New York City metropolitan statistical area has the largest [foreign-born population of any metropolitan region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foreign_born#Metropolitan_regions_with_largest_foreign_born_populations \"Foreign born\") in the world. The New York region continues to be by far the leading metropolitan gateway for legal immigrants admitted into the United States, substantially exceeding the combined totals of Los Angeles and [Miami](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami_metropolitan_area \"Miami metropolitan area\").[[266]](#cite_note-Immigrants2022est-273) Nearly seven times as many young professionals applied for jobs in New York City in 2023 as compared to 2019, making New York the most popular destination for recent college graduates.[[267]](#cite_note-NYCMostPopularDestinationCollegeGrads-274)\n\nThe New York metropolitan area became the [world's largest urban area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World's_largest_city \"World's largest city\") in 1925, surpassing [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London \"London\").[[268]](#cite_note-275)[[269]](#cite_note-Chandler-276) The metropolitan area surpassed 10 million in the early 1930s, becoming the first [megacity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Megacity \"Megacity\").[[127]](#cite_note-:1-130)[[269]](#cite_note-Chandler-276) In 1955, it was surpassed by the [Greater Tokyo Area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greater_Tokyo_Area \"Greater Tokyo Area\").[[270]](#cite_note-277)[[269]](#cite_note-Chandler-276)\n\n### Ethnicity and nationality\n\nMain articles: [Race and ethnicity in New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race_and_ethnicity_in_New_York_City \"Race and ethnicity in New York City\") and [New York City ethnic enclaves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City_ethnic_enclaves \"New York City ethnic enclaves\")\n\nAccording to 2022 estimates from the [American Community Survey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Community_Survey \"American Community Survey\"), the largest self-reported ancestries in New York City were [Jamaican](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamaican_Americans \"Jamaican Americans\") (2.4%), [Ecuadorian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecuadorian_Americans \"Ecuadorian Americans\") (2.3%), (1.1%).[[271]](#cite_note-United_States_Census_Bureau-278)[[13]](#cite_note-The_City_of_New_York-15)[[14]](#cite_note-Digital_Diplomacy_Coalition,_New_York-16)\n\n| Historical demographics | approximately 36.3% of the city's population is [foreign-born](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foreign-born \"Foreign-born\") (compared to 13.7% nationwide),[[256]](#cite_note-QuickFacts-263) and 40% of all children are born to mothers who are immigrants.[[274]](#cite_note-281) Throughout its history, New York has been a major [port of entry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_of_entry \"Port of entry\") for immigrants.[[275]](#cite_note-CityDiversity-282)[[276]](#cite_note-NYC_immigration-283) No single country or region of origin dominates.[[275]](#cite_note-CityDiversity-282) Queens has the largest Asian-American and [Andean populations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andean_civilizations \"Andean civilizations\") in the United States, and is also the most ethnically and linguistically diverse urban area in the world.[[27]](#cite_note-QueensMostLinguisticallyDiverseTop-30)[[189]](#cite_note-QueensMostDiverseWorld2-192) The wider New York City metropolitan region is home to the world's largest [foreign-born population of any metropolitan region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foreign_born#Metropolitan_and_urban_regions_with_the_largest_foreign-born_populations \"Foreign born\"), enumerating 5.9 million as of 2023.\n\n[New York City ethnic enclaves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City_ethnic_enclaves \"New York City ethnic Manhattan\n\n[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e4/Little_Italy_NY_Street.JPG/250px-Little_Italy_NY_Street.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Little_Italy_NY_Street.JPG)\n\n[Little Italy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Little_Italy,_Manhattan \"Little Italy, Manhattan\"), Manhattan\n\n[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/45/Brighton_beach_%287434138858%29.jpg/250px-Brighton_beach_%287434138858%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Brighton_beach_(7434138858).jpg)\n\n[Little Russia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brighton_Beach#Russian-speaking_culture \"Brighton Beach\"), Brooklyn\n\n[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/14/74th_St_shopping_Jax_Hts_jeh.jpg/250px-74th_St_shopping_Jax_Hts_jeh.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:74th_St_shopping_Jax_Hts_jeh.jpg)\n\n[Little India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jackson_Heights,_Queens \"Jackson Heights, Queens\"), Queens\n\nThe [New York metropolitan area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_metropolitan_area \"New York metropolitan area\") has the largest [Asian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asians_in_New_York_City \"Asians in New York City\") population, at 2.6 million.[[277]](#cite_note-NYCMetroLargestAsianPopulation-284) New York has the largest [Chinese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_people_in_the_New_York_metropolitan_area \"Chinese people in the New York metropolitan area\") population outside of Asia and [Asian Indian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asian_Indian \"Asian Indian\") population in the Western Hemisphere,[[278]](#cite_note-NYCLargestChinesePopulation-285) as well as the largest [Russian-American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian-American \"Russian-American\"),[[279]](#cite_note-U.S._Department_of_Homeland_Security-286) Italian-American, and African-American populations. New York is home to the largest [Dominican-American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominican-American \"Dominican-American\"), [Puerto Rican–American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puerto_Rican_migration_to_New_York_City \"Puerto Rican migration to New York City\"), and [South American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_American_Americans \"South American Americans\")[[279]](#cite_note-U.S._Department_of_Homeland_Security-286) and the second-largest overall [Hispanic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hispanic_and_Latino_American \"Hispanic and Latino American\") population in the United States, numbering over 5 million. [Venezuela](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venezuelan_Americans \"Venezuelan Americans\"), [Ecuador](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecuadorian_Americans \"Ecuadorian Americans\"), [Colombia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombian_Americans \"Colombian Americans\"), [Guyana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guyanese_Americans \"Guyanese Americans\"), [Peru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peruvian_Americans \"Peruvian Americans\"), and [Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazilian_Americans \"Brazilian Americans\"), are the top source countries from South America for immigrants to the New York City region; the [Dominican Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominican_Republic \"Dominican Republic\"), [Jamaica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamaica \"Jamaica\"), [Haiti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haiti \"Haiti\"), and [Trinidad and Tobago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trinidadian_and_Tobagonian_Americans \"Trinidadian and Tobagonian Americans\") in the [Caribbean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caribbeans_in_New_York_City \"Caribbeans in New York City\"); [Nigeria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigerian_Americans \"Nigerian Americans\"), [Egypt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egyptian_Americans \"Egyptian Americans\"), [Ghana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghanaian_Americans \"Ghanaian Americans\"), [Tanzania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tanzanian_Americans \"Tanzanian Americans\"), [Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenyan_Americans \"Kenyan Americans\"), and [South Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_African_Americans \"South African Americans\") from [Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_immigration_to_the_United_States \"African immigration to the United States\"); and [El Salvador](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salvadoran_Americans \"Salvadoran Americans\"), [Honduras](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honduran_Americans \"Honduran Americans\"), and [Guatemala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guatemalan_Americans \"Guatemalan Americans\") in Central America.[[280]](#cite_note-287)\n\nNew York City contains the highest total Asian population of any U.S. city proper.[[281]](#cite_note-288) [Asian Americans in New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asian_Americans_in_New_York_City \"Asian Americans in New York City\"), according to the 2010 census, number more than 1.2 million,[[256]](#cite_note-QuickFacts-263) greater than the combined totals of San Francisco and Los Angeles.[[282]](#cite_note-289) [Manhattan's Chinatown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manhattan's_Chinatown \"Manhattan's Chinatown\") is the highest concentration of Chinese people in the [Western Hemisphere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Hemisphere \"Western Hemisphere\"),[[283]](#cite_note-fact-sheet-290) and Queens is home to the largest [Tibetan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tibetan_people \"Tibetan people\") population outside Asia.[[284]](#cite_note-UnreachedNY-291) [Arab Americans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arab_Americans \"Arab Americans\") number over 160,000 in New York City,[[285]](#cite_note-292) with the highest concentration in Brooklyn. New York City hosts the highest [Palestinian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palestinian_Americans \"Palestinian Americans\") population in the United States,[[286]](#cite_note-NYCLargestPalestinianPopulation-293) and the highest diasporas of [Uzbek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uzbek_American \"Uzbek American\") and [Albanian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albanian_Americans \"Albanian Americans\") diasporas in the world;[[287]](#cite_note-NYCWhiteMuslimDiasporas-294) [Turkish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkish_American \"Turkish American\"), [Armenian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armenian_Americans \"Armenian Americans\"), and [Azerbaijani Americans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Azerbaijani_Americans \"Azerbaijani Americans\") are also rapidly growing segments of the city's non-Hispanic White population.[[288]](#cite_note-NYCLittleIstanbul-295)[[289]](#cite_note-296)[[290]](#cite_note-297) The metropolitan area is home to 20% of the nation's [Indian Americans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indians_in_the_New_York_City_metropolitan_region \"Indians in the New York City metropolitan region\") and at least twenty [Little India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Little_India \"Little India\") enclaves, and 15% of all [Korean Americans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korean_Americans_in_New_York_City \"Korean Americans in New York City\") and four [Koreatowns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koreatown,_Manhattan \"Koreatown, Manhattan\").[[291]](#cite_note-NYCAmericanCommunitySurvey-298) New York City and its metropolitan area have the largest population of [Blacks or African Americans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Americans_in_New_York_City \"African Americans in New York City\") in the nation.[[292]](#cite_note-299)\n\nNew York City has the largest [European](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_American \"European American\") and [non-Hispanic white](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-Hispanic_white \"Non-Hispanic white\") population of any American city, numbering 2.7 million in 2012.[[293]](#cite_note-300) The [European diaspora](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_diaspora \"European diaspora\") residing in the city is very diverse and many [European ethnic groups have formed enclaves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City_ethnic_enclaves#European \"New York City ethnic enclaves\").[[294]](#cite_note-BrightonBeachRussianSpeakingEpicenter-301)[[295]](#cite_note-AstoriaNYCGreektown1-302)[[296]](#cite_note-AstoriaNYCGreektown2-303) With 960,000 Jewish inhabitants as of 2023, New York City is home to the highest [Jewish population](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jewish_population_by_city \"Jewish population by city\") of any city in the world,[[297]](#cite_note-Gergely-2024-304) and its metropolitan area concentrated over 2 million Jews as of 2021, the second largest Jewish population worldwide after the [Tel Aviv metropolitan area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tel_Aviv_metropolitan_area \"Tel Aviv metropolitan area\") in Israel.[[298]](#cite_note-305) In the borough of Brooklyn, an estimated one in four residents was Jewish as of 2018.[[299]](#cite_note-BrookynTheMostJewishSpotOnEarth-306)\n\n### Sexual orientation and gender identity\n\nMain articles: [LGBTQ culture in New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LGBTQ_culture_in_New_York_City \"LGBTQ culture in New York City\"), [Transgender culture of New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transgender_culture_of_New_York_City \"Transgender culture of New York City\"), [Same-sex marriage in New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_New_York \"Same-sex marriage in New York\"), and [NYC Pride March](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NYC_Pride_March \"NYC Pride March\")\n\nFurther information: [New York City Drag March](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City_Drag_March \"New York City Drag March\"), [Queens Pride Parade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queens_Pride_Parade \"Queens Pride Parade\"), [List of LGBT people from New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_LGBT_people_from_New_York_City \"List of LGBT people from New York City\"), and [List of largest LGBT events](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_largest_LGBT_events \"List of largest LGBT events\")\n\nNew York City has been described as the [gay capital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LGBT_culture_in_New_York_City \"LGBT culture in New York City\") of the world and the central node of the [lesbian, gay, bisexual, and transgender](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lesbian,_gay,_bisexual,_and_transgender \"Lesbian, gay, bisexual, and transgender\") (LGBT) [sociopolitical ecosystem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Political_sociology \"Political sociology\"), and is home to one of the world's largest LGBT populations and the most prominent.[[300]](#cite_note-NYCGayCapitalOfTheWorld1-307) The New York metropolitan area is home to about 570,000 self-identifying [gay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gays_in_New_York_City \"Gays in New York City\") and [bisexual](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bisexual \"Bisexual\") people, [the largest in the country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LGBT_demographics_of_the_United_States#By_metropolitan_area \"LGBT demographics of the United States\").[[301]](#cite_note-308)[[302]](#cite_note-309) Same-sex sexual activity between consenting adults has been legal in New York since 1980's *[New York v. Onofre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_v._Onofre \"New York v. Onofre\")* case, which invalidated the state's [sodomy law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sodomy_laws_in_the_United_States#State_and_territorial_laws_prior_to_Lawrence_v._Texas \"Sodomy laws in the United States\").[[303]](#cite_note-310) [Same-sex marriage in New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_New_York \"Same-sex marriage in New York\") was legalized on June 24, 2011, and the new law took effect on July 23, 2011.[[304]](#cite_note-311)\n\n[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d7/NYC_Pride_2019_26.jpg/250px-NYC_Pride_2019_26.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:NYC_Pride_2019_26.jpg)\n\nThe [NYC Pride March](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NYC_Pride_March \"NYC Pride March\") is the [largest pride parade in the world](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_largest_LGBT_events \"List of largest LGBT events\").[[305]](#cite_note-NYCWorld'sLargestPrideParade-312)\n\nThe annual [NYC Pride March](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NYC_Pride_March \"NYC Pride March\") proceeds southward down [Fifth Avenue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifth_Avenue \"Fifth Avenue\") and ends at [Greenwich Village](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greenwich_Village \"Greenwich Village\") in Lower Manhattan; the parade is the [largest pride parade in the world](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_largest_LGBT_events \"List of largest LGBT events\"), attracting tens of thousands of participants and millions of sidewalk spectators each June.[[305]](#cite_note-NYCWorld'sLargestPrideParade-312)[[306]](#cite_note-NYCWorld-313) The annual [Queens Pride Parade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queens_Pride_Parade \"Queens Pride Parade\") is held in [Jackson Heights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jackson_Heights \"Jackson Heights\") and is accompanied by the ensuing *Multicultural Parade*.[[307]](#cite_note-NYCTrans-314)\n\n[Stonewall 50 – WorldPride NYC 2019](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stonewall_50_–_WorldPride_NYC_2019 \"Stonewall 50 – WorldPride NYC 2019\") was the [largest international Pride celebration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_largest_LGBT_events \"List of largest LGBT events\") in history, commemorating the 50th anniversary of the Stonewall uprising, with 150,000 participants and five million spectators attending in Manhattan alone.[[308]](#cite_note-Authorities1-315) New York City is home to the largest [transgender](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transgender \"Transgender\") population in the world, estimated at more than 50,000 in 2018, concentrated in Manhattan, Brooklyn, and Queens; however, until the June 1969 Stonewall riots, this community had felt marginalized and neglected by the gay community.[[307]](#cite_note-NYCTrans-314)[[138]](#cite_note-TransEqualityNYC-141) Brooklyn Liberation March, the largest [transgender-rights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transgender_rights \"Transgender rights\") demonstration in LGBT history, took place on June 14, 2020, stretching from [Grand Army Plaza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Army_Plaza \"Grand Army Plaza\") to [Fort Greene, Brooklyn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Greene,_Brooklyn \"Fort Greene, Brooklyn\"), focused on supporting Black transgender lives, drawing an estimated 15,000 to 20,000 participants.[[309]](#cite_note-316)[[310]](#cite_note-317)\n\n### Religion\n\nFurther information: [St. Patrick's Cathedral (Midtown Manhattan)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Cathedral_(Midtown_Manhattan) \"St. Patrick's Cathedral (Midtown Manhattan)\"), [Rockefeller Center Christmas City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_the_Jews_in_New_York_City \"History of the Jews in New York City\"), [Jewish arrival in New Amsterdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jewish_arrival_in_New_Amsterdam \"Jewish arrival in New Amsterdam\"), [Islam in New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islam_in_New_York_City \"Islam in New York City\"), [Hindu Temple Society of North America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindu_Temple_Society_of_North_America \"Hindu Temple Society of North America\"), [Mahayana Buddhism North America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahayana_Buddhism_North_America \"Mahayana Buddhism North America\"), and [Falun Gong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Falun_Gong \"Falun Gong\")\n\nNotable religious buildings in New York City\n\n[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3e/Emanu-elNYjeh.JPG/250px-Emanu-elNYjeh.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Emanu-elNYjeh.JPG)\n\n[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/03/At_New_York%2C_USA_2017_119.jpg/120px-At_New_York%2C_USA_2017_119.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:At_New_York,_USA_2017_119.jpg)\n\n[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/76/Islamic_Cultural_Center_E96_jeh.JPG/250px-Islamic_Cultural_Center_E96_jeh.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Islamic_Cultural_Center_E96_jeh.JPG)\n\n[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1f/Hindu_Temple_Society_of_North_America_%28Flushing%2C_Queens_-_exterior%29.jpg/120px-Hindu_Temple_Society_of_North_America_%28Flushing%2C_Queens_-_exterior%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Hindu_Temple_Society_of_North_America_(Flushing,_Queens_-_exterior).jpg)\n\nLeft to right from the top: The [Temple Emanu-El](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Temple_Emanu-El_of_New_York_(1930) \"Temple Emanu-El of New York (1930)\"); [St. Patrick's Cathedral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Cathedral_(New_York_City) \"St. Patrick's Cathedral (New York City)\"); [Islamic Cultural Center of New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamic_Cultural_Center_of_New_York \"Islamic Cultural Center of New York\"); and [Hindu Temple Society of North America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindu_Temple_Society_of_North_America \"Hindu Temple Society of North America\")\n\n[Christianity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christianity_in_the_United_States \"Christianity in the United States\") is the largest religion (59% adherent) in New York City,[[311]](#cite_note-NYCReligion1-318) which is home to the highest number of churches of any city in the world.[[16]](#cite_note-NYCTheCapitaloftheWorld-18) [Catholicism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholicism \"Catholicism\") is the largest Christian denomination (33%), followed by [Protestantism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protestantism \"Protestantism\") (23%), and [other Christian denominations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Christian_denominations \"List of Christian denominations\") (3%). The [Latin Catholic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin_Catholic \"Latin Catholic\") population is primarily served by the [Roman Catholic Archdiocese of New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_Catholic_Archdiocese_of_New_York \"Roman Catholic Archdiocese of New York\") and [Diocese of Brooklyn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diocese_of_Brooklyn \"Diocese of Brooklyn\"), while [Eastern Catholics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Catholics \"Eastern Catholics\") are divided into numerous jurisdictions throughout the city. [Evangelical Protestantism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evangelical_Protestantism \"Evangelical Protestantism\") is the largest branch of Protestantism in the city (9%), followed by [Mainline Protestantism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mainline_Protestant \"Mainline Protestant\") (8%), while the converse is usually true for other U.S. cities and metropolitan areas.[[312]](#cite_note-NYCReligion2-319)\n\nWith [960,000 Jewish inhabitants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jews_in_New_York_City \"Jews in New York City\") as of 2023, [Judaism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judaism \"Judaism\") is the second-largest religion practiced in New York City,[[297]](#cite_note-Gergely-2024-304) which is home to the largest Jewish population outside of [Tel Aviv](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tel_Aviv \"Tel Aviv\"). Nearly half of the city's Jewish population lives in Brooklyn.[[313]](#cite_note-BrooklynJewish-320)[[299]](#cite_note-BrookynTheMostJewishSpotOnEarth-306)\n\n[Islam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islam \"Islam\") ranks as the third-largest religion in New York City, following Christianity and Judaism, with estimates ranging between 600,000 and 1,000,000 observers of Islam, including 10% of the city's public school children.[[314]](#cite_note-321) 22.3% of [American Muslims](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Muslims \"American Muslims\") live in New York City, with 1.5 million Muslims in the greater [New York metropolitan area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_metropolitan_area \"New York metropolitan area\"), the largest metropolitan Muslim population in the [Western Hemisphere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Hemisphere \"Western Hemisphere\")[[315]](#cite_note-322)—and the most [ethnically diverse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethnically_diverse \"Ethnically diverse\") Muslim population of any city in the world.[[316]](#cite_note-NYCMostDiverseMuslimPopulationWorld-323) [Powers Street Mosque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Powers_Street_Mosque \"Powers Street Mosque\") in Brooklyn is one of the oldest continuously operating mosques in the United States, and represents the first Islamic organization in both the city and the state.[[317]](#cite_note-324)[[318]](#cite_note-325)\n\nFollowing these three largest religious groups in New York City are [Hinduism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hinduism \"Hinduism\"), [Buddhism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buddhism \"Buddhism\"), [Sikhism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sikhism \"Sikhism\"), [Zoroastrianism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zoroastrianism \"Zoroastrianism\"), and others. As of 2023, 24% of Greater New Yorkers identified with no organized religious affiliation, and 4% were self-identified [atheists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atheist \"Atheist\").[[319]](#cite_note-NYCReligion3-326)\n\n## Economy\n\nMain article: [Economy of New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economy_of_New_York_City \"Economy of New York City\")\n\n[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/73/Midtown_Manhattan_from_Weehawken_September_2021_001.jpg/250px-Midtown_Manhattan_from_Weehawken_September_2021_001.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Midtown_Manhattan_from_Weehawken_September_2021_001.jpg)\n\n[Midtown Manhattan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midtown_Manhattan \"Midtown Manhattan\") is the world's largest central business district.[[32]](#cite_note-reuters-2022-03-24-35)\n\n [![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d8/Lower_Manhattan_skyline_from_Upper_New_York_Bay%2C_20231001_1031_0838.jpg/250px-Lower_Manhattan_skyline_from_Upper_New_York_Bay%2C_20231001_1031_0838.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Lower_Manhattan_skyline_from_Upper_New_York_Bay,_20231001_1031_0838.jpg)\n\n[Lower Manhattan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lower_Manhattan \"Lower Manhattan\"), including [Wall Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wall_Street \"Wall Street\"), the world's principal financial center,[[320]](#cite_note-NYCFinancialAndFintechCapitalWorld-327) and [One World Trade Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One_World_Trade_Center \"One World Trade Center\"), the tallest skyscraper in the [Western Hemisphere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Hemisphere \"Western Hemisphere\")\n\nNew York City is a global hub of business and commerce, sometimes called the \"Capital of the World\".[[321]](#cite_note-NewYorkCapitaloftheWorld1-328) Greater New York is the [world's largest metropolitan economy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_cities_by_GDP \"List of cities by GDP\"), with a [gross metropolitan product](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gross_metropolitan_product \"Gross metropolitan product\") estimated at US$2.16 trillion in
