2022.[[7]](#cite_note-bea.gov-8)[[8]](#cite_note-fred.stlouisfed.org-9) New York is a center for worldwide banking and finance, health care, and [life sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Life_sciences \"Life sciences\"),[[322]](#cite_note-NYCHealthCareLifeSciences-329) [medical technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medical_technology \"Medical technology\") and research, retailing, world trade, transportation, tourism, real estate, [new media](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_media \"New media\"), [traditional media](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Traditional_media \"Traditional media\"), advertising, [legal services](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legal_services \"Legal services\"), [accountancy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Accountancy \"Accountancy\"), insurance, and the arts in the United States; while [Silicon Alley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silicon_Alley \"Silicon Alley\"), [metonymous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metonymous \"Metonymous\") for New York's high technology sphere, continues to expand. The [Port of New York and New Jersey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_of_New_York_and_New_Jersey \"Port of New York and New Jersey\") is a major economic engine, benefitting [post-Panamax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panamax \"Panamax\") from the expansion of the [Panama Canal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panama_Canal \"Panama Canal\").[[323]](#cite_note-330)[[324]](#cite_note-331)[[325]](#cite_note-332)\n\nMany [*Fortune* 500](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fortune_500 \"Fortune 500\") corporations are headquartered in New York City,[[326]](#cite_note-333) as are a large number of [multinational corporations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multinational_corporation \"Multinational corporation\"). New York City has been ranked first among cities across the globe in attracting [capital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capital_(economics) \"Capital (economics)\"), business, and tourists.[[327]](#cite_note-334)[[328]](#cite_note-335) New York City's role as the top global center for the [advertising industry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Advertising \"Advertising\") is metonymously reflected as *[Madison Avenue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madison_Avenue#Advertising_industry \"Madison Avenue\")*.[[329]](#cite_note-MadisonAveMetonym-336) The city's [fashion industry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fashion_industry \"Fashion industry\") provides approximately 180,000 employees with $11 billion in annual wages.[[330]](#cite_note-337)\n\nSignificant other economic sectors include universities and non-profit institutions. [Manufacturing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manufacturing_in_the_United_States \"Manufacturing in the United States\") declined over the 20th century but still accounts for significant employment. The city's apparel and [garment industry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garment_industry \"Garment industry\"), historically centered on the [Garment District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garment_District,_Manhattan \"Garment District, Manhattan\") in Manhattan, peaked in 1950, when more than 323,000 workers were employed in the industry in New York. In 2015, fewer than 23,000 New York City residents were employed in the industry, although revival efforts were underway,[[331]](#cite_note-338) and the American fashion industry continues to be metonymized as *[Seventh Avenue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seventh_Avenue_(Manhattan) \"Seventh Avenue (Manhattan)\")*.[[332]](#cite_note-339)\n\nIn 2024, the gross domestic product of New York City exceeded US$1.3 trillion, of which over $1 trillion (77%) was produced by [Manhattan alone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_U.S._counties_by_GDP \"List of U.S. counties by GDP\").[[333]](#cite_note-ManhattanGDP-340)[[7]](#cite_note-bea.gov-8) Like other large cities, New York City has a degree of [income disparity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Income_disparity \"Income disparity\"), as indicated by its [Gini coefficient](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gini_coefficient \"Gini coefficient\") of 0.55 as of 2022.[[334]](#cite_note-341)[[335]](#cite_note-342) In November 2023, the city had total employment of over 4.75 million of which more than a quarter were in education and health services.[[336]](#cite_note-343) Manhattan, which accounted for more than half of the city's jobs, had an average weekly wage of $2,590 in the second quarter of 2023, ranking fourth-highest among the nation's 360 largest counties.[[337]](#cite_note-BLS2023Q3-344) New York City is one of the relatively few American cities levying an [income tax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Income_tax \"Income tax\") (about 3%) on its residents;[[338]](#cite_note-Localities_with_INCOME_tax-345)[[339]](#cite_note-NYCTax-346)[[340]](#cite_note-NYC_tax_schedule-347) despite this tax levy, New York City in 2024 was home by a significant margin to the highest number of billionaires of any city in the world, with a total of 110.[[41]](#cite_note-NYCHighestNumberBillionaires-44)\n\n### Wall Street\n\nMain articles: [Wall Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wall_Street \"Wall Street\") and [Financial District, Manhattan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Financial_District,_Manhattan \"Financial District, Manhattan\")\n\n[![A large flag is stretched over Roman-style columns on the front of a large building.](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/26/Gaming-Wall-Street_BTS_Prodigium-266.jpg/250px-Gaming-Wall-Street_BTS_Prodigium-266.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Gaming-Wall-Street_BTS_Prodigium-266.jpg)\n\nThe [New York Stock Exchange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Stock_Exchange \"New York Stock Exchange\") is the [world's largest stock exchange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_stock_exchanges#Major_stock_exchanges \"List of stock exchanges\") per total [market capitalization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Market_capitalization \"Market capitalization\") of [its listed companies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lists_of_companies_listed_on_the_New_York_Stock_Exchange \"Lists of companies listed on the New York Stock Exchange\").[[341]](#cite_note-NYSElargest-348)[[342]](#cite_note-NYSEhighestcap-349)\n\nNew York City's most important [economic sector](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economic_sector \"Economic sector\") lies in its role as a comprehensive [financial center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Financial_center \"Financial center\"), metonymously known as *Wall Street*. [Lower Manhattan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lower_Manhattan \"Lower Manhattan\") is home to the [New York Stock Exchange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Stock_Exchange \"New York Stock Exchange\") and the [Nasdaq](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nasdaq \"Nasdaq\"), representing the world's largest and second largest [stock exchanges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stock_exchange \"Stock exchange\"), respectively, when measured both by overall average daily trading volume and by total [market capitalization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Market_capitalization \"Market capitalization\") of their listed companies in 2013.[[341]](#cite_note-NYSElargest-348)[[342]](#cite_note-NYSEhighestcap-349) In fiscal year 2013–14, Wall Street's [securities industry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Securities_industry \"Securities industry\") generated 19% of New York State's tax revenue.[[343]](#cite_note-350)\n\nNew York City remains the largest global center for trading in [public equity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_equity \"Public equity\") and [debt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Security_(finance) \"Security (finance)\") capital markets.[[344]](#cite_note-CNY2007-351): 31–32[[345]](#cite_note-352) New York also leads in [hedge fund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hedge_fund \"Hedge fund\") management; [private equity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_private_equity_firms \"List of private equity firms\"); and the monetary volume of [mergers and acquisitions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mergers_and_acquisitions \"Mergers and acquisitions\"). Several [investment banks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Investment_banks \"Investment banks\") and [investment managers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Investment_managers \"Investment managers\") headquartered in Manhattan are important participants in other global financial centers.[[344]](#cite_note-CNY2007-351): 34–35 New York is the principal [commercial banking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commercial_bank \"Commercial bank\") center of the United States.[[346]](#cite_note-353)\n\nManhattan contained over 500 million square feet (46.5 million m2) of office space in 2018,[[347]](#cite_note-ManhattanOfficeSpace-354) making New York City the largest office market in the world,[[348]](#cite_note-355)[[349]](#cite_note-356) while [Midtown Manhattan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midtown_Manhattan \"Midtown Manhattan\"), with 400 million square feet (37.2 million m2) in 2018,[[347]](#cite_note-ManhattanOfficeSpace-354) is the largest central business district in the world.[[350]](#cite_note-357)\n\n### Tech and biotech\n\nFurther information: [Tech:NYC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tech:NYC \"Tech:NYC\"), [Tech companies in New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tech_companies_in_New_York_City \"Tech companies in New York City\"), [Biotech companies in New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biotech_companies_in_New_York_City \"Biotech companies in New York City\"), and [Silicon Alley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silicon_Alley \"Silicon Alley\")\n\n[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/67/Flatiron_District.jpg/250px-Flatiron_District.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Flatiron_District.jpg)\n\nThe [Flatiron District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flatiron_District \"Flatiron District\") is the cradle of Silicon Alley, initially metonymous for the New York metropolitan region's high tech sector.\n\n [![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/05/Cornell_Tech_buildings_%2841991%29.jpg/250px-Cornell_Tech_buildings_%2841991%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Cornell_Tech_buildings_(41991).jpg)\n\n[Cornell Tech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cornell_Tech \"Cornell Tech\") on [Roosevelt Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roosevelt_Island \"Roosevelt Island\")\n\nNew York is a top-tier global technology hub.[[351]](#cite_note-NewYorkCityDestinationNumberOneTechHub-358)[[352]](#cite_note-NYCTopTierTechHub-359) As of 2025, the [New York metropolitan area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_metropolitan_area \"New York metropolitan area\") has become the largest [tech talent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software_engineering \"Software engineering\") hub in the world.[[9]](#cite_note-NYCLargestTechTalentHubWorld-11) Silicon Alley, once a metonym for the sphere encompassing the metropolitan region's [high technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High_tech \"High tech\") industries,[[353]](#cite_note-Dickey2013-360) is no longer a relevant moniker as the city's tech environment has expanded dramatically both in location and in scope since at least 2003, when tech business appeared in more places in Manhattan and other boroughs, and not much [silicon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silicon \"Silicon\") was involved.[[353]](#cite_note-Dickey2013-360)[[354]](#cite_note-Ward2018-361) New York City's current tech sphere encompasses the array of applications involving universal applications of [artificial intelligence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_intelligence \"Artificial intelligence\") (AI),[[355]](#cite_note-AI-NYC1A-362)[[356]](#cite_note-AI-NYC1B-363) broadband internet,[[357]](#cite_note-364) [new media](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_media \"New media\"), [financial technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Financial_technology \"Financial technology\") (*fintech*) and [cryptocurrency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cryptocurrency \"Cryptocurrency\"), [biotechnology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biotechnology \"Biotechnology\"), [game design](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_design \"Game design\"), and other fields within information technology that are supported by its [entrepreneurship ecosystem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Entrepreneurship_ecosystem \"Entrepreneurship ecosystem\") and [venture capital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venture_capital \"Venture capital\") investments. Technology-driven [startup companies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Startup_companies \"Startup companies\") and entrepreneurial employment are growing in New York City and the region. The technology sector has been claiming a greater share of New York City's economy since 2010.[[358]](#cite_note-TechNYC1-365) [Tech:NYC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tech:NYC \"Tech:NYC\"), founded in 2016, is a non-profit organization which represents New York City's technology industry with government, civic institutions, in business, and in the media, and whose primary goals are to further augment New York's substantial tech talent base and to advocate for policies that will nurture tech companies to grow in the city.[[359]](#cite_note-366)\n\nNew York City's AI sector raised US$483.6 million in venture capital investment in 2022.[[360]](#cite_note-NYCArtificialIntelligenceHub-367) In 2023, New York unveiled the first comprehensive initiative to create both a framework of rules and a [chatbot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chatbot \"Chatbot\") to regulate the use of AI within the sphere of city government.[[361]](#cite_note-NYCArtificialIntelligenceGovernment-368)\n\nThe [biotechnology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biotech_and_pharmaceutical_companies_in_the_New_Jersey/New_York_metropolitan_region \"Biotech and pharmaceutical companies in the New Jersey/New York metropolitan region\") sector is growing in New York City, based on the city's strength in academic [scientific research](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_research \"Scientific research\") and public and commercial financial support. On December 19, 2011, Mayor Michael R. Bloomberg announced his choice of [Cornell University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cornell_University \"Cornell University\") and [Technion-Israel Institute of Technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Technion-Israel_Institute_of_Technology \"Technion-Israel Institute of Technology\") to build a $2 billion graduate school of [applied sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Applied_science \"Applied science\") called [Cornell Tech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cornell_Tech \"Cornell Tech\") on [Roosevelt Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roosevelt_Island \"Roosevelt Island\") intending to transform New York City into the world's premier technology capital.[[362]](#cite_note-369)[[363]](#cite_note-370)\n\n### Real estate\n\n[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c3/5th_Avenue_9304.JPG/250px-5th_Avenue_9304.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:5th_Avenue_9304.JPG)\n\n[Fifth Avenue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifth_Avenue \"Fifth Avenue\") in [Midtown Manhattan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midtown_Manhattan \"Midtown Manhattan\") is the most expensive shopping street in the world.[[364]](#cite_note-FifthAvenueMostExpensiveStreetOnEarth-371)\n\nNew York City real estate is a haven for global investors.[[36]](#cite_note-NYCSafeHavenGlobalInvestors-39) The total value of all New York City property was assessed at US$1.479 trillion for the 2017 [fiscal year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fiscal_year \"Fiscal year\"), an increase of 6.1% from the previous year. Of the total market value, single family homes accounted for $765 billion (51.7%); [condominiums](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Condominium \"Condominium\"), [co-ops](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Housing_cooperative \"Housing cooperative\"), and apartment buildings totaled $351 billion (23.7%); and commercial properties were valued at $317 billion (21.4%).[[365]](#cite_note-372)[[366]](#cite_note-NYC_real_estate-373) [Fifth Avenue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifth_Avenue \"Fifth Avenue\") in Midtown Manhattan commands the highest retail rents in the world, at $2,000 per square foot ($22,000/m2) in 2023.[[367]](#cite_note-374)\n\nNew York City has one of the highest [costs of living](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Costs_of_living \"Costs of living\") in the world, which is exacerbated by the city's housing shortage.[[368]](#cite_note-375)[[369]](#cite_note-376) In 2023, one-bedroom apartments in Manhattan rented at a median monthly price of US$4,443.[[370]](#cite_note-377) The median house price city-wide is over $1 million as of 2023.[[371]](#cite_note-378) With 33,000 units available in 2023 among the city's 2.3 million rentable apartments, the vacancy rate was 1.4%, the lowest level since 1968 and a rate that is indicative of a shortage of available units, especially among those with rents below a monthly rental of $1,650, where less than 1% of units were available.[[372]](#cite_note-379) Perennially high demand has pushed median monthly one-bedroom apartment rents in New York City to over US$4,000 and two-bedroom rents to over $5,000, the highest in the United States by a significant margin.[[373]](#cite_note-NYCMostExpensiveRents-380)\n\n### Tourism\n\nMain article: [Tourism in New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tourism_in_New_York_City \"Tourism in New York City\")\n\n[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/07/Times_Square%2C_Broadway%2C_May_2016.jpg/250px-Times_Square%2C_Broadway%2C_May_2016.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Times_Square,_Broadway,_May_2016.jpg)\n\n[Times Square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times_Square \"Times Square\") is one of the world's leading tourist attractions with 50 million tourists annually.[[232]](#cite_note-NYCvisitors-238)\n\nTourism is a vital industry for New York City, and New York City Tourism + Conventions represents the city's official bureau of tourism.[[374]](#cite_note-381) New York has witnessed a growing combined volume of international and domestic tourists, with as many as 66.6 million visitors to the city per year, including as many as 13.5 million international visitors, with the highest numbers from the United Kingdom, Canada, Brazil, and China.[[375]](#cite_note-Tourism2021-382) Multiple sources have called New York the most photographed city in the world.[[376]](#cite_note-NYCMostPhotographed1-383)[[377]](#cite_note-NYCMostPhotographed2-384)[[378]](#cite_note-NYCMostPhotographed3-385) *[I Love New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Love_New_York \"I Love New York\")* (stylized I ❤ NY) is both a logo and a song that are the basis of an [advertising campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Advertising_campaign \"Advertising campaign\") and have been used since 1977 to promote [tourism in New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tourism_in_New_York_City \"Tourism in New York City\"),[[379]](#cite_note-386) and later to promote New York State as well. The trademarked logo is owned by [New York State Empire State Development](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_State_Empire_State_Development \"New York State Empire State Development\").[[380]](#cite_note-387)\n\nMany [districts and monuments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lists_of_New_York_City_landmarks \"Lists of New York City landmarks\") in New York City are major landmarks, including three of the world's ten most-visited tourist attractions in 2023.[[381]](#cite_note-388) A record 66.6 million tourists visited New York City in 2019, bringing in $47.4 billion in tourism revenue. Visitor numbers dropped by two-thirds in 2020 during the pandemic, rebounding to 63.3 million in 2023.[[375]](#cite_note-Tourism2021-382)[[382]](#cite_note-389) Major landmarks in New York City include the [Metropolitan Museum of Art](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolitan_Museum_of_Art \"Metropolitan Museum of Art\"), the [Statue of Liberty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Liberty \"Statue of Liberty\"), the [Empire State Building](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Empire_State_Building \"Empire State Building\"), and Central Park.[[383]](#cite_note-390) Times Square is the brightly illuminated hub of the [Broadway Theater District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broadway_Theater_District \"Broadway Theater District\"),[[384]](#cite_note-391) and a major center of the world's [entertainment industry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Entertainment_industry \"Entertainment industry\"),[[385]](#cite_note-392) attracting 50 million visitors annually to one of the world's busiest pedestrian intersections.[[232]](#cite_note-NYCvisitors-238) According to [The Broadway League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Broadway_League \"The Broadway League\"), shows on [Broadway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broadway_theatre \"Broadway theatre\") sold approximately US$1.54 billion worth of tickets in both the 2022–2023 and the 2023–2024 seasons. Both seasons featured theater attendance of approximately 12.3 million each.[[386]](#cite_note-BroadwayLeagueStatistics-393)\n\n### Media and entertainment\n\nMain article: [Media in New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Media_in_New_York_City \"Media in New York City\")\n\nFurther information: [New Yorkers in journalism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Yorkers_in_journalism \"New Yorkers in journalism\")\n\n[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/ce/New_York%2C_2019_%2848621790492%29.jpg/250px-New_York%2C_2019_%2848621790492%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:New_York,_2019_(48621790492).jpg)\n\n[Rockefeller Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rockefeller_Center \"Rockefeller Center\"), one of Manhattan's leading [media and entertainment hubs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Media_in_New_York_City \"Media in New York City\")\n\n [![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/94/Freedom_Of_Speech_%28256854761%29.jpeg/250px-Freedom_Of_Speech_%28256854761%29.jpeg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Freedom_Of_Speech_(256854761).jpeg)\n\n[The headquarters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_York_Times_Building \"The New York Times Building\") of [the New York Times Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_York_Times_Company \"The New York Times Company\"), publisher of *[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_York_Times \"The New York Times\")*\n\nNew York City has been described as the [entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Show_business \"Show business\")[[16]](#cite_note-NYCTheCapitaloftheWorld-18)[[387]](#cite_note-NYCTheEntertainmentCapitaloftheWorld-394)[[388]](#cite_note-395) and [digital media](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_media \"Digital media\") capital of the world.[[389]](#cite_note-396) It is a center for the advertising, [music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_of_New_York_City \"Music of New York City\"), [newspaper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_New_York_City_newspapers_and_magazines \"List of New York City newspapers and magazines\"), digital media, and publishing industries, and is the largest media market in North America.[[390]](#cite_note-397) Many of the world's largest [media conglomerates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Media_conglomerate \"Media conglomerate\") are based in the city, including [Warner Bros. Discovery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Bros._Discovery \"Warner Bros. Discovery\"), the [Thomson Reuters Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomson_Reuters_Corporation \"Thomson Reuters Corporation\"), the [Associated Press](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Associated_Press \"Associated Press\"), [Bloomberg L.P.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bloomberg_L.P. \"Bloomberg L.P.\"), the [News Corp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/News_Corp \"News Corp\"), [The New York Times Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_York_Times_Company \"The New York Times Company\"), [NBCUniversal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBCUniversal \"NBCUniversal\"), the [Hearst Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hearst_Corporation \"Hearst Corporation\"), [AOL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AOL \"AOL\") and [Fox Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fox_Corporation \"Fox Corporation\"). Seven of the world's top eight global [advertising agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Advertising_agency \"Advertising agency\") networks have their headquarters in New York.[[391]](#cite_note-398)\n\nMore than 200 newspapers and 350 consumer magazines have an office in the city,[[392]](#cite_note-NYC_Media-399) and the publishing industry employs about 11,500 people, with an economic impact of $9.2 billion.[[393]](#cite_note-400) The two national daily newspapers with the largest daily [circulations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circulation_(newspaper) \"Circulation (newspaper)\") in the United States are published in New York: *[The Wall Street Journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Wall_Street_Journal \"The Wall Street Journal\")* and *[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_York_Times \"The New York Times\")* broadsheets.[[394]](#cite_note-401) With 132 awards through 2022, *The Times* has won the most [Pulitzer Prizes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pulitzer_Prize \"Pulitzer Prize\") for journalism[[395]](#cite_note-402) and is considered the U.S. media's [newspaper of record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newspaper_of_record \"Newspaper of record\").[[396]](#cite_note-403) [Tabloid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tabloid_(newspaper_format) \"Tabloid (newspaper format)\") newspapers in the city include the *[New York Daily News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Daily_News \"New York Daily News\")*, which was founded in 1919 by [Joseph Medill Patterson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph_Medill_Patterson \"Joseph Medill Patterson\"),[[397]](#cite_note-404) and the *[New York Post](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Post \"New York Post\")*, founded in 1801 by [Alexander Hamilton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_Hamilton \"Alexander Hamilton\").[[398]](#cite_note-405)[[399]](#cite_note-406)\n\nAs of 2019[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=New_York_City&action=edit), New York City was the second-largest center for filmmaking and television production in the United States, producing about 200 feature films annually. The industry employed more than 100,000 people in 2019, generating $12.2 billion in wages and a total economic impact of $64.1 billion.[[400]](#cite_note-407) By volume, New York is the world leader in [independent film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Independent_film \"Independent film\") production—one-third of all American independent films are produced there.[[401]](#cite_note-408)[[392]](#cite_note-NYC_Media-399)\n\nNew York is a major center for [non-commercial educational](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-commercial_educational \"Non-commercial educational\") media. [NYC Media](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NYC_Media \"NYC Media\") is the official public radio, television, and online media network and broadcasting service of New York City,[[402]](#cite_note-409) and has produced several original [Emmy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emmy_Award \"Emmy Award\")-winning shows covering music and culture in city neighborhoods and city government. The oldest [public-access television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public-access_television \"Public-access television\") channel in the United States is the [Manhattan Neighborhood Network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manhattan_Neighborhood_Network \"Manhattan Neighborhood Network\"), founded in 1971.[[403]](#cite_note-410) [WNET](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WNET \"WNET\") is the city's major public television station and produces a third of national [Public Broadcasting Service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_Broadcasting_Service \"Public Broadcasting Service\") (PBS) television programming.[[404]](#cite_note-411) [WNYC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WNYC \"WNYC\"), a [public radio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_radio \"Public radio\") station owned by the city until 1997,[[405]](#cite_note-412) has the largest public radio audience in the United States.[[406]](#cite_note-413)\n\n## Education\n\nMain article: [Education in New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Education_in_New_York_City \"Education in New York City\")\n\n[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5d/Low_Memorial_Library_Columbia_University_College_Walk_Court_Yard_05.jpg/250px-Low_Memorial_Library_Columbia_University_College_Walk_Court_Yard_05.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Low_Memorial_Library_Columbia_University_College_Walk_Court_Yard_05.jpg)\n\nThe [Low Memorial Library](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Low_Memorial_Library \"Low Memorial Library\") at [Columbia University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_University \"Columbia University\")\n\nNew York City has the largest educational system of any city.[[16]](#cite_note-NYCTheCapitaloftheWorld-18) The city's educational infrastructure spans primary education, secondary education, higher education, and research. The [New York City Public Schools](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City_Public_Schools \"New York City Public Schools\") system, managed by the [New York City Department of Education](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City_Department_of_Education \"New York City Department of Education\"), is the largest public school system in the United States, serving about 1.1 million students in approximately 1,800 separate primary and secondary schools, including [charter schools](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charter_schools \"Charter schools\"), as of 2017–2018.[[407]](#cite_note-414) There are approximately 900 additional privately run secular and religious schools.[[408]](#cite_note-415)\n\n[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/02/Facade_of_the_New_York_Public_Library_Main_Branch_2.jpg/250px-Facade_of_the_New_York_Public_Library_Main_Branch_2.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Facade_of_the_New_York_Public_Library_Main_Branch_2.jpg)\n\nThe [Stephen A. Schwarzman Headquarters Building](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Public_Library_Main_Branch \"New York Public Library Main Branch\") of the [New York Public Library](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Public_Library \"New York Public Library\")\n\nThe [New York Public Library](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Public_Library \"New York Public Library\") (NYPL) has the largest collection of any public library system in the United States.[[409]](#cite_note-libraryspot-416) Queens is served by the [Queens Borough Public Library](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queens_Borough_Public_Library \"Queens Borough Public Library\") (QPL), the nation's second-largest public library system, while the [Brooklyn Public Library](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brooklyn_Public_Library \"Brooklyn Public Library\") (BPL) serves Brooklyn.[[409]](#cite_note-libraryspot-416)\n\nMore than a million students, the highest number of any city in the United States,[[410]](#cite_note-417) are enrolled in New York City's more than 120 higher education institutions, with nearly a quarter million in the [City University of New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_University_of_New_York \"City University of New York\") (CUNY) system alone as of 2025[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=New_York_City&action=edit).[[411]](#cite_note-418)\n\nThe public CUNY system comprises 25 institutions across all five boroughs.[[412]](#cite_note-419) The public [State University of New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_University_of_New_York \"State University of New York\") (SUNY) system's campuses in New York City include [SUNY Downstate Health Sciences University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SUNY_Downstate_Health_Sciences_University \"SUNY Downstate Health Sciences University\"), [Fashion Institute of Technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fashion_Institute_of_Technology \"Fashion Institute of Technology\"), [SUNY Maritime College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SUNY_Maritime_College \"SUNY Maritime College\"), and [SUNY College of Optometry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SUNY_College_of_Optometry \"SUNY College of Optometry\").[[413]](#cite_note-420) New York City is home to such notable private universities as [Adelphi University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adelphi_University \"Adelphi University\"), [Bank Street College of Education](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_Street_College_of_Education \"Bank Street College of Education\"), [Barnard College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barnard_College \"Barnard College\"), [Columbia University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_University \"Columbia University\"), [Cooper Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cooper_Union \"Cooper Union\"), [Fordham University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fordham_University \"Fordham University\"), [New York University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_University \"New York University\"), [New York Institute of Technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Institute_of_Technology \"New York Institute of Technology\"), [Rockefeller University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rockefeller_University \"Rockefeller University\"), [Mercy University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercy_University \"Mercy University\"), [Cornell Tech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cornell_Tech \"Cornell Tech\") and [Yeshiva University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yeshiva_University \"Yeshiva University\"); several of these are ranked among the top universities in the world,[[414]](#cite_note-ARWU-421)[[415]](#cite_note-CWUR-422) while some of the world's most prestigious institutions, such as [Princeton University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Princeton_University \"Princeton University\") and [Yale University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yale_University \"Yale University\"), are in the [New York metropolitan area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_metropolitan_area \"New York metropolitan area\").\n\nMuch of the [scientific research](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_research \"Scientific research\") in the city is done in medicine and the [life sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Life_sciences \"Life sciences\"). In 2019, the New York metropolitan area ranked first [by share of published articles in life sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_cities_by_scientific_output#Leading_cities_in_different_fields \"List of cities by scientific output\").[[416]](#cite_note-NYCLifeSciencesCapital-423) New York City has the most postgraduate life sciences degrees awarded annually in the United States, and in 2012, 43,523 licensed physicians were practicing in New York City.[[417]](#cite_note-424) There are 127 [Nobel laureates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_laureate \"Nobel laureate\") with roots in local institutions as of 2004[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=New_York_City&action=edit).[[418]](#cite_note-NYC_science_institutions-425)\n\n## Culture\n\nMain article: [Culture of New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Culture_of_New_York_City \"Culture of New York City\")\n\n[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6b/NYC_-_Guggenheim_Museum.jpg/250px-NYC_-_Guggenheim_Museum.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:NYC_-_Guggenheim_Museum.jpg)\n\n[Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solomon_R._Guggenheim_Museum \"Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum\") seen from Fifth Avenue\n\nNew York City is frequently the [setting for novels, movies, and television programs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_films_set_in_New_York_City \"List of films set in New York City\") and has been described as the cultural capital of the world.[[419]](#cite_note-cultura1-426)[[420]](#cite_note-culture2-427)[[421]](#cite_note-culture3-428)[[422]](#cite_note-cultural4-429) The city is the birthplace of many cultural movements, including the [Harlem Renaissance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harlem_Renaissance \"Harlem Renaissance\") in literature and visual art;[[423]](#cite_note-430)[[424]](#cite_note-431) [abstract expressionism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abstract_expressionism \"Abstract expressionism\") (known as the [New York School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_School_(art) \"New York School (art)\")) in painting; and [hip-hop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hip-hop \"Hip-hop\"),[[195]](#cite_note-Toop-1992-198)[[425]](#cite_note-BPOHPINY-432) [punk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punk_rock \"Punk rock\"),[[426]](#cite_note-433) [hardcore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hardcore_punk \"Hardcore punk\"),[[427]](#cite_note-434) [salsa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salsa_music \"Salsa music\"), [freestyle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freestyle_music \"Freestyle music\"), [Tin Pan Alley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tin_Pan_Alley \"Tin Pan Alley\"), certain forms of [jazz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jazz \"Jazz\"),[[428]](#cite_note-Jazzzz-435) and (along with Philadelphia) [disco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disco \"Disco\") in music. New York City has been considered the dance capital of the world.[[429]](#cite_note-436)[[430]](#cite_note-437)\n\n### Pace\n\n[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3d/Broadway_%289075158922%29.jpg/250px-Broadway_%289075158922%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Broadway_(9075158922).jpg)\n\nNew York is typically characterized by its fast pace of life,[[18]](#cite_note-FastPaceNYC1-21)[[19]](#cite_note-FastPaceNYC2-22)[[20]](#cite_note-FastPaceNYC3-23) which has spawned the term *[New York minute](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/New%20York%20minute \"wiktionary:New York minute\")*.[[431]](#cite_note-NewYorkMinuteDefinition-438)\n\nOne of the most common traits attributed to New York City is its fast pace,[[18]](#cite_note-FastPaceNYC1-21)[[19]](#cite_note-FastPaceNYC2-22)[[20]](#cite_note-FastPaceNYC3-23) which spawned the term *[New York minute](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/New%20York%20minute \"wiktionary:New York minute\")*.[[431]](#cite_note-NewYorkMinuteDefinition-438) New York City's residents are prominently known for their resilience historically, and more recently related to their management of the impacts of the [September 11 terrorist attacks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/September_11_terrorist_attacks \"September 11 terrorist attacks\") and the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_New_York_City \"COVID-19 pandemic in New York City\").[[432]](#cite_note-439)[[433]](#cite_note-Weaver-2022-440)[[434]](#cite_note-441) New York was voted the world's most resilient city in 2021 and 2022, per [*Time Out*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_Out_(magazine) \"Time Out (magazine)\")'s global poll of urban residents.[[433]](#cite_note-Weaver-2022-440)\n\n### Theater\n\nFurther information: [Broadway theater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broadway_theater \"Broadway theater\") and [Theater District, Manhattan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theater_District,_Manhattan \"Theater District, Manhattan\")\n\n[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/cd/Various_Pictures_from_New_York_City_-_September%2C_2025.jpg/250px-Various_Pictures_from_New_York_City_-_September%2C_2025.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Various_Pictures_from_New_York_City_-_September,_2025.jpg)\n\nThe [Golden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Golden_Theatre \"John Golden Theatre\"); [Jacobs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_B._Jacobs_Theatre \"Bernard B. Jacobs Theatre\"); [Schoenfeld](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerald_Schoenfeld_Theatre \"Gerald Schoenfeld Theatre\"); and [Booth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Booth_Theatre \"Booth Theatre\") theaters in the [Theater District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theater_District,_Manhattan \"Theater District, Manhattan\")\n\nThe central [hub of the American theater scene is Manhattan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theater_District,_Manhattan \"Theater District, Manhattan\"), with its divisions of [Broadway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broadway_theatre \"Broadway theatre\"), [off-Broadway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Off-Broadway \"Off-Broadway\"), and [off-off-Broadway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Off-off-Broadway \"Off-off-Broadway\").[[435]](#cite_note-LondréWatermeier1998-442) Many stage and screen [stars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity \"Celebrity\") have gotten their big break working in New York productions.[[436]](#cite_note-443)\n\nBroadway theater is one of the premier forms of English-language theater in the world, named after [Broadway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broadway_(Manhattan) \"Broadway (Manhattan)\"), the major thoroughfare that crosses [Times Square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times_Square \"Times Square\"),[[437]](#cite_note-444) sometimes referred to as \"[The Great White Way](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Great_White_Way \"The Great White Way\")\".[[438]](#cite_note-445)[[439]](#cite_note-446)[[440]](#cite_note-447)\n\n[Forty-one theaters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Broadway_theaters \"List of Broadway theaters\"), mostly in Midtown Manhattan's [Theater District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theater_District,_Manhattan \"Theater District, Manhattan\"), each with at least 500 seats, are classified as Broadway theaters.[[441]](#cite_note-448) The 2018–19 Broadway theater season set records with total attendance of 14.8 million and gross revenue of $1.83 billion[[442]](#cite_note-449) Recovering from [closures forced by the COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impact_of_the_COVID-19_pandemic_on_the_performing_arts#Live_music_and_theatre \"Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the performing arts\"), 2022–23 revenues rebounded to $1.58 billion with total attendance of 12.3 million.[[443]](#cite_note-450)[[386]](#cite_note-BroadwayLeagueStatistics-393) The [Tony Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Awards \"Tony Awards\") recognize excellence in live Broadway theater and are presented annually by the [American Theatre Wing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Theatre_Wing \"American Theatre Wing\") and [The Broadway League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Broadway_League \"The Broadway League\")[[444]](#cite_note-451) in Manhattan.[[445]](#cite_note-452)\n\n### Accent and dialect\n\nMain articles: [New York City English](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City_English \"New York City English\") and [New York accent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_accent \"New York accent\")\n\nThe New York area is home to a distinctive regional accent and speech pattern called the [New York dialect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_dialect \"New York dialect\"), alternatively known as *Brooklynese* or *New Yorkese*. It has been considered one of the most recognizable accents within [American English](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_English \"American English\").[[446]](#cite_note-453) The traditional New York area speech pattern is known for its rapid delivery, and its accent is characterized as [non-rhotic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-rhotic \"Non-rhotic\") so that the sound [ɹ] does not appear at the end of a [syllable](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syllable \"Syllable\") or immediately before a [consonant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Consonant \"Consonant\"), therefore the pronunciation of the city name as \"New Yawk\".[[447]](#cite_note-NYT19930214-454) The classic version of the New York City dialect is centered on [middle-](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middle_class \"Middle class\") and working-class New Yorkers. The influx of non-European immigrants in recent decades has led to changes in this distinctive dialect,[[447]](#cite_note-NYT19930214-454) and the traditional form of this speech pattern is no longer as prevalent.[[447]](#cite_note-NYT19930214-454)\n\n### Architecture\n\nMain article: [Architecture of New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Architecture_of_New_York_City \"Architecture of New York City\")\n\nFurther information: [List of buildings, sites, and monuments in New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_buildings,_sites,_and_monuments_in_New_York_City \"List of buildings, sites, and monuments in New York City\") and [List of tallest buildings in New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_tallest_buildings_in_New_York_City \"List of tallest buildings in New York City\")\n\n[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3f/1232-42_Dean_Street_Crown_Heights.jpg/250px-1232-42_Dean_Street_Crown_Heights.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:1232-42_Dean_Street_Crown_Heights.jpg)\n\n[Row houses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Row_houses \"Row houses\") in [Crown Heights North Historic District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crown_Heights_North_Historic_District \"Crown Heights North Historic District\"), Brooklyn\n\nNew York has architecturally noteworthy buildings in a wide range of styles and from distinct periods, from the Dutch Colonial [Pieter Claesen Wyckoff House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyckoff_House \"Wyckoff House\") in Brooklyn, the oldest section of which dates to 1656, to the modern [One World Trade Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One_World_Trade_Center \"One World Trade Center\"), the skyscraper at [Ground Zero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Trade_Center_site \"World Trade Center site\") in Lower Manhattan and the [most expensive office tower in the world](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_most_expensive_buildings_in_the_world \"List of most expensive buildings in the world\") by construction cost.[[448]](#cite_note-455)\n\nManhattan's [skyline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skyline \"Skyline\"), with its many skyscrapers, has been recognized as an iconic symbol of the city,[[449]](#cite_note-456)[[450]](#cite_note-457)[[451]](#cite_note-458) and the city has been home to several of the [tallest buildings in the world](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skyscraper#History_of_the_tallest_skyscrapers \"Skyscraper\"). As of 2019[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=New_York_City&action=edit), New York City had 6,455 high-rise buildings, the third most in the world after [Hong Kong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hong_Kong \"Hong Kong\") and [Seoul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seoul \"Seoul\").[[452]](#cite_note-459)\n\nThe character of New York's large residential districts is often defined by the elegant [brownstone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brownstone \"Brownstone\") rowhouses and [townhouses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Townhouse \"Townhouse\") and shabby [tenements](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenement \"Tenement\") that were built during a period of rapid expansion from 1870 to 1930.[[453]](#cite_note-460) Stone and brick became the city's building materials of choice after the construction of wood-frame houses was limited in the aftermath of the [Great Fire of 1835](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Fire_of_New_York \"Great Fire of New York\").[[454]](#cite_note-lankevich-p82-461)\n\nIn contrast, New York City also has neighborhoods that are less densely populated and feature free-standing dwellings. In neighborhoods such as [Riverdale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale,_Bronx \"Riverdale, Bronx\") (in the Bronx), [Ditmas Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ditmas_Park \"Ditmas Park\") (in Brooklyn), and [Douglaston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douglaston \"Douglaston\") (in Queens), large single-family homes are common in various architectural styles such as [Tudor Revival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tudor_Revival \"Tudor Revival\") and [Victorian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victorian_architecture \"Victorian architecture\").[[455]](#cite_note-462)[[456]](#cite_note-463)[[457]](#cite_note-464)\n\n[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ef/Midtown_Manhattan_from_Weehawken_September_2021_HDR_panorama.jpg/1280px-Midtown_Manhattan_from_Weehawken_September_2021_HDR_panorama.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Midtown_Manhattan_from_Weehawken_September_2021_HDR_panorama.jpg \"High-resolution panorama of Midtown Manhattan, taken from Weehawken, New Jersey, on September 2021\")\n\nHigh-resolution panorama of [Midtown Manhattan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midtown_Manhattan \"Midtown Manhattan\"), taken from [Weehawken, New Jersey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weehawken,_New_Jersey \"Weehawken, New Jersey\"), on September 2021\n\n### Arts\n\nFurther information: [List of museums and cultural institutions in New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_museums_and_cultural_institutions_in_New_York_City \"List of museums and cultural institutions in New York City\") and [Music of New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_of_New_York_City \"Music of New York City\")\n\n[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/01/Lincoln_Center_at_dawn.jpg/250px-Lincoln_Center_at_dawn.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Lincoln_Center_at_dawn.jpg)\n\nThe [Lincoln Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lincoln_Center \"Lincoln Center\"): [David H. Koch Theater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_H._Koch_Theater \"David H. Koch Theater\") (left), home of the [NY City Ballet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City_Ballet \"New York City Ballet\"); [Metropolitan Opera House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolitan_Opera_House_(Lincoln_Center) \"Metropolitan Opera House (Lincoln Center)\") (center), home of the [Metropolitan Opera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolitan_Opera \"Metropolitan Opera\"); and [David Geffen Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Geffen_Hall \"David Geffen Hall\") (right), home of the [NY Philharmonic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NY_Philharmonic \"NY Philharmonic\")\n\n [![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/30/Metropolitan_Museum_of_Art_%28The_Met%29_-_Central_Park%2C_NYC.jpg/250px-Metropolitan_Museum_of_Art_%28The_Met%29_-_Central_Park%2C_NYC.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Metropolitan_Museum_of_Art_(The_Met)_-_Central_Park,_NYC.jpg)\n\n[Metropolitan Museum of Art](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolitan_Museum_of_Art \"Metropolitan Museum of Art\"), the largest [art museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Art_museum \"Art museum\") in the Americas\n\n[Lincoln Center for the Performing Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lincoln_Center_for_the_Performing_Arts \"Lincoln Center for the Performing Arts\"), anchoring [Lincoln Square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lincoln_Square,_Manhattan \"Lincoln Square, Manhattan\") on the Upper West Side of Manhattan, is home to numerous influential arts organizations, including the [Metropolitan Opera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolitan_Opera \"Metropolitan Opera\"), [New York City Opera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City_Opera \"New York City Opera\"), [New York Philharmonic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Philharmonic \"New York Philharmonic\"), and [New York City Ballet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City_Ballet \"New York City Ballet\"), as well as the [Vivian Beaumont Theater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vivian_Beaumont_Theater \"Vivian Beaumont Theater\"), the [Juilliard School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juilliard_School \"Juilliard School\"), [Jazz at Lincoln Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jazz_at_Lincoln_Center \"Jazz at Lincoln Center\"), and [Alice Tully Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alice_Tully_Hall \"Alice Tully Hall\"). The [Lee Strasberg Theatre and Film Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lee_Strasberg_Theatre_and_Film_Institute \"Lee Strasberg Theatre and Film Institute\") is in [Union Square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Union_Square_(New_York_City) \"Union Square (New York City)\"), and [Tisch School of the Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tisch_School_of_the_Arts \"Tisch School of the Arts\") is based at New York University, while [Central Park SummerStage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Park_SummerStage \"Central Park SummerStage\") presents free concerts in Central Park.[[458]](#cite_note-465)\n\nNew York City has more than 2,000 arts and cultural organizations and more than 500 [art galleries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Art_galleries \"Art galleries\").[[459]](#cite_note-NYC_arts-466) The city government funds the arts with a larger annual budget than the [National Endowment for the Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Endowment_for_the_Arts \"National Endowment for the Arts\").[[459]](#cite_note-NYC_arts-466) The city is also home to hundreds of cultural institutions and historic sites. [Museum Mile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifth_Avenue \"Fifth Avenue\") is the name for a section of Fifth Avenue running from 82nd to 105th streets on the [Upper East Side](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Upper_East_Side \"Upper East Side\") of Manhattan,[[460]](#cite_note-festival-467) in the upper portion of [Carnegie Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carnegie_Hill \"Carnegie Hill\").[[461]](#cite_note-468)\n\nNine museums occupy this section of Fifth Avenue, including the [Guggenheim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solomon_R._Guggenheim_Museum \"Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum\"), [Metropolitan Museum of Art](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolitan_Museum_of_Art \"Metropolitan Museum of Art\"), [Neue Galerie New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neue_Galerie_New_York \"Neue Galerie New York\"), the [Jewish Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jewish_Museum_(Manhattan) \"Jewish Museum (Manhattan)\"), and [The Africa Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Africa_Center \"The Africa Center\"), making it one of the densest displays of [high culture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High_culture \"High culture\") in the world.[[462]](#cite_note-mmilemus-469) In addition to other programming, the museums collaborate for the annual Museum Mile Festival, held each year in June, to promote the museums and increase visitation.[[463]](#cite_note-drv-470) Many of the world's most lucrative [art auctions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Art_auction \"Art auction\") are held in New York City.[[464]](#cite_note-NYCArtAuction1-471)[[465]](#cite_note-NYCArtAuction2-472)\n\nThe Metropolitan Museum of Art is the [largest art museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_largest_art_museums \"List of largest art museums\") in the Americas. In 2022, it welcomed 3.2 million visitors, ranking it the [third-most visited museum in the country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_most-visited_museums_in_the_United_States \"List of most-visited museums in the United States\"), and [eighth-most visited art museum in the world](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_most-visited_art_museums \"List of most-visited art museums\").[[466]](#cite_note-473) Its permanent collection contains more than two million works across 17 curatorial departments,[[467]](#cite_note-Metropolitan_Museum_Launches_New_and_Expanded_Web_Site-474) and includes works of art from [classical antiquity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Classical_antiquity \"Classical antiquity\") and [ancient Egypt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Art_of_ancient_Egypt \"Art of ancient Egypt\"); paintings and sculptures from nearly all the [European masters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_painting \"Western painting\"); and an extensive collection of [American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visual_art_of_the_United_States \"Visual art of the United States\") and [modern art](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_art \"Modern art\"). The Met maintains extensive holdings of [African](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_art \"African art\"), [Asian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asian_art \"Asian art\"), [Oceanian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oceanian_art \"Oceanian art\"), [Byzantine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Byzantine_art \"Byzantine art\"), and [Islamic art](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamic_art \"Islamic art\").[[468]](#cite_note-475)\n\n### Cuisine\n\nMain articles: [Cuisine of New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuisine_of_New_York_City \"Cuisine of New York City\"), [List of restaurants in New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_restaurants_in_New_York_City \"List of restaurants in New York City\"), and [List of Michelin-starred restaurants in New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Michelin-starred_restaurants_in_New_York_City \"List of Michelin-starred restaurants in New York City\")\n\n[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0a/Lox-and-bagel-02.jpg/250px-Lox-and-bagel-02.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Lox-and-bagel-02.jpg)\n\n[New York–style bagel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York–style_bagel \"New York–style bagel\") with [lox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lox \"Lox\")\n\nNew York City's food culture includes an array of international cuisines influenced by the city's long immigrant history. [Central](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Europe \"Central Europe\") and Eastern European immigrants, especially [Jewish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jewish_Americans \"Jewish Americans\") immigrants from those regions, brought [New York-style bagels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York-style_bagel \"New York-style bagel\"), [cheesecake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheesecake#North_America \"Cheesecake\"), [hot dogs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hot_dog \"Hot dog\"), [knishes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knish \"Knish\"), and [delicatessens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delicatessen \"Delicatessen\") (delis) to the city. [Italian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_diaspora \"Italian diaspora\") immigrants brought [New York-style pizza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York-style_pizza \"New York-style pizza\") and [Italian cuisine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_cuisine \"Italian cuisine\") into the city, while Jewish immigrants and Irish immigrants brought [pastrami](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pastrami \"Pastrami\")[[469]](#cite_note-476) and [corned beef](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corned_beef \"Corned beef\"),[[470]](#cite_note-477) respectively. [Chinese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_restaurant \"Chinese restaurant\") and other Asian restaurants, sandwich joints, [trattorias](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trattoria \"Trattoria\"), [diners](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diner \"Diner\"), and [coffeehouses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coffeehouse \"Coffeehouse\") are ubiquitous throughout the city. Some 4,000 mobile food vendors licensed by the city, many immigrant-owned, have made Middle Eastern foods such as [falafel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Falafel \"Falafel\") and [kebabs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kebab \"Kebab\")[[471]](#cite_note-478) examples of modern New York [street food](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Street_food \"Street food\"). The city is home to \"nearly one thousand of the finest and most diverse [haute cuisine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haute_cuisine \"Haute cuisine\") restaurants in the world\", according to [Michelin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michelin \"Michelin\").[[472]](#cite_note-479) The [New York City Department of Health and Mental Hygiene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City_Department_of_Health_and_Mental_Hygiene \"New York City Department of Health and Mental Hygiene\") assigns letter grades to the city's restaurants based on inspection results.[[473]](#cite_note-480) As of 2019, there were 27,043 restaurants in the city, up from 24,865 in 2017.[[474]](#cite_note-481) The [Queens Night Market](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queens_Night_Market \"Queens Night Market\") in [Flushing Meadows–Corona Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flushing_Meadows–Corona_Park \"Flushing Meadows–Corona Park\") attracts more than ten thousand people nightly to sample food from more than 85 countries.[[306]](#cite_note-NYCWorld-313)\n\n### Fashion\n\nFurther information: [New York Fashion Week](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Fashion_Week \"New York Fashion Week\") and [Met Gala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Met_Gala \"Met Gala\")\n\n[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a6/Carolina_Herrera_AW14_12.jpg/250px-Carolina_Herrera_AW14_12.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Carolina_Herrera_AW14_12.jpg)\n\n[Haute couture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haute_couture \"Haute couture\") fashion models walk the [runway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catwalk \"Catwalk\") during [NYFW](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NYFW \"NYFW\").\n\nNew York City is a global [fashion capital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fashion_capital \"Fashion capital\"), and the [fashion industry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fashion \"Fashion\") employs 4.6% of the city's private workforce.[[475]](#cite_note-NYCFashionCapital-482) [New York Fashion Week](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Fashion_Week \"New York Fashion Week\") (NYFW) is a high-profile semiannual event featuring [models](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fashion_model \"Fashion model\") displaying the latest wardrobes created by fashion designers worldwide in advance of these fashions proceeding to the marketplace.[[476]](#cite_note-NewYorkFashionWeekRetailTrendsetter-483)\n\nNYFW sets the tone for the global fashion industry.[[477]](#cite_note-NewYorkFashionWeekGlobalAndEconomicImpact-484) New York's fashion district encompasses roughly 30 city blocks in [Midtown Manhattan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midtown_Manhattan \"Midtown Manhattan\"),[[478]](#cite_note-NYCFashionDistrict-485) clustered around a stretch of [Seventh Avenue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seventh_Avenue_(Manhattan) \"Seventh Avenue (Manhattan)\") nicknamed *[Fashion Avenue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seventh_Avenue_(Manhattan)#Notable_districts_and_buildings \"Seventh Avenue (Manhattan)\")*.[[479]](#cite_note-NYCFashionAvenue-486) New York's fashion calendar also includes Couture Fashion Week to showcase [haute couture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haute_couture \"Haute couture\") styles.[[480]](#cite_note-NYCHauteCouture-487) The Met Gala is often described as \"Fashion's biggest night\".[[481]](#cite_note-MetGalaFashion'sBiggestNight-488)\n\n### Parades\n\nFurther information: [List of parades in New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Category:Parades_in_New_York_City \"Category:Parades in New York City\")\n\n[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/30/Macy%27s_Thanksgiving_Day_Parade_2022_New_York_City_%2852523112564%29.jpg/250px-Macy%27s_Thanksgiving_Day_Parade_2022_New_York_City_%2852523112564%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Macy's_Thanksgiving_Day_Parade_2022_New_York_City_(52523112564).jpg)\n\nThe annual [Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Macy's_Thanksgiving_Day_Parade \"Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade\"), the world's largest parade[[482]](#cite_note-NYCThanksgivingParadeLargestWorld-489)\n\nNew York City is well known for its street [parades](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parade \"Parade\"), the majority in Manhattan. The primary orientation of the annual street parades is typically from north to south, marching along major avenues. The annual [Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Macy's_Thanksgiving_Day_Parade \"Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade\") is the world's largest parade,[[482]](#cite_note-NYCThanksgivingParadeLargestWorld-489) beginning alongside Central Park and proceeding southward to the flagship [Macy's Herald Square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Macy's_Herald_Square \"Macy's Herald Square\") store;[[483]](#cite_note-490) the parade is viewed on telecasts worldwide and draws millions of spectators in person.[[482]](#cite_note-NYCThanksgivingParadeLargestWorld-489) Other notable parades include the annual [New York City St. Patrick's Day Parade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City_St._Patrick's_Day_Parade \"New York City St. Patrick's Day Parade\") in March, the [NYC LGBT Pride March](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NYC_LGBT_Pride_March \"NYC LGBT Pride March\") in June, the LGBT-inspired [Greenwich Village Halloween Parade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greenwich_Village_Halloween_Parade \"Greenwich Village Halloween Parade\") in October, and numerous parades commemorating the independence days of many nations. [Ticker-tape parades](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_ticker-tape_parades_in_New_York_City \"List of ticker-tape parades in New York City\") celebrating championships won by sports teams as well as other accomplishments march northward along the [Canyon of Heroes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canyon_of_Heroes \"Canyon of Heroes\") on [Broadway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broadway_(Manhattan) \"Broadway (Manhattan)\") from [Bowling Green](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bowling_Green_(New_York_City) \"Bowling Green (New York City)\") to [City Hall Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_Hall_Park \"City Hall Park\") in Lower Manhattan.\n\n### Sports\n\nMain articles: [Sports in the New York metropolitan area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sports_in_the_New_York_metropolitan_area \"Sports in the New York metropolitan area\") and [Traditional games of New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Traditional_games_of_New_York_City \"Traditional games of New York City\")\n\n[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/29/Arthur_ashe_stadium_interior.jpg/250px-Arthur_ashe_stadium_interior.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Arthur_ashe_stadium_interior.jpg)\n\nThe [US Open Tennis Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/US_Open_Tennis_Championships \"US Open Tennis Championships\") in [Flushing Meadows–Corona Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flushing_Meadows–Corona_Park \"Flushing Meadows–Corona Park\") in [Queens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queens \"Queens\")\n\n[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8d/Citi_Field_2011.JPG/250px-Citi_Field_2011.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Citi_Field_2011.JPG)\n\n[Citi Field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citi_Field \"Citi Field\"), also in Flushing Meadows-Corona Park, has been home to the [New York Mets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Mets \"New York Mets\") since 2009.\n\n[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/af/Yankee_Stadium_overhead_2010.jpg/250px-Yankee_Stadium_overhead_2010.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Yankee_Stadium_overhead_2010.jpg)\n\n[Yankee Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yankee_Stadium \"Yankee Stadium\") in [The Bronx](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bronx \"The Bronx\") is home to the [New York Yankees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Yankees \"New York Yankees\") and [New York City FC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City_FC \"New York City FC\").\n\n[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4a/Barclays_Center_1.jpg/250px-Barclays_Center_1.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Barclays_Center_1.jpg)\n\n[Barclays Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barclays_Center \"Barclays Center\"), home to the [Brooklyn Nets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brooklyn_Nets \"Brooklyn Nets\") of the [NBA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA \"NBA\") and the [New York Liberty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Liberty \"New York Liberty\") of the [WNBA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WNBA \"WNBA\")\n\n[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4b/Madison_Square_Garden_%28MSG%29_-_Full_%2848124330357%29.jpg/250px-Madison_Square_Garden_%28MSG%29_-_Full_%2848124330357%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Madison_Square_Garden_(MSG)_-_Full_(48124330357).jpg)\n\n[Madison Square Garden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madison_Square_Garden \"Madison Square Garden\"), home to the [New York Knicks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Knicks \"New York Knicks\") of the NBA and [New York Rangers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Rangers \"New York Rangers\") of the [NHL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NHL \"NHL\")\n\nNew York City is home to the headquarters of the [National Football League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_League \"National Football League\"),[[484]](#cite_note-491) [Major League Baseball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball \"Major League Baseball\"),[[485]](#cite_note-492) the [National Basketball Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Basketball_Association \"National Basketball Association\"),[[486]](#cite_note-493) the [National Hockey League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Hockey_League \"National Hockey League\"),[[487]](#cite_note-494) and [Major League Soccer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Soccer \"Major League Soccer\").[[488]](#cite_note-495)\n\nNew York City hosted the [1984 Summer Paralympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1984_Summer_Paralympics \"1984 Summer Paralympics\")[[489]](#cite_note-496) and the [1998 Goodwill Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1998_Goodwill_Games \"1998 Goodwill Games\").[[490]](#cite_note-497) New York City's [bid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City_bid_for_the_2012_Summer_Olympics \"New York City bid for the 2012 Summer Olympics\") to host the [2012 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics \"2012 Summer Olympics\") was one of five finalists, but lost out to London.[[491]](#cite_note-498)\n\nThe city has played host to more than 40 major professional teams in the five sports and their respective competing leagues. Four of the ten most expensive stadiums ever built worldwide ([MetLife Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MetLife_Stadium \"MetLife Stadium\"), the new [Yankee Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yankee_Stadium \"Yankee Stadium\"), [Madison Square Garden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madison_Square_Garden \"Madison Square Garden\"), and [Citi Field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citi_Field \"Citi Field\")) are in the New York metropolitan area.[[492]](#cite_note-499)\n\nThe city is represented in the National Football League by the [New York Giants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Giants \"New York Giants\") and the [New York Jets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Jets \"New York Jets\"), although both teams play their home games at MetLife Stadium in nearby [East Rutherford, New Jersey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Rutherford,_New_Jersey \"East Rutherford, New Jersey\"),[[493]](#cite_note-500) which hosted [Super Bowl XLVIII](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLVIII \"Super Bowl XLVIII\") in 2014.[[494]](#cite_note-501)\n\nThe city's two Major League Baseball teams are the [New York Mets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Mets \"New York Mets\"), who play at 41,800-seat Citi Field in Queens, and the [New York Yankees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Yankees \"New York Yankees\"), who play at 47,400-seat [Yankee Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yankee_Stadium \"Yankee Stadium\") in the Bronx.[[495]](#cite_note-502) The [two rivals compete](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mets–Yankees_rivalry \"Mets–Yankees rivalry\") in six games of [interleague play](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interleague_play \"Interleague play\") every regular season, called the [Subway Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subway_Series \"Subway Series\").[[496]](#cite_note-503) The Yankees have won an MLB-record 27 championships,[[497]](#cite_note-504) while the Mets have won the [World Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Series \"World Series\") twice.[[498]](#cite_note-505) The city was once home to the Brooklyn Dodgers (now the [Los Angeles Dodgers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Dodgers \"Los Angeles Dodgers\")), who won the World Series once,[[499]](#cite_note-506) and the [New York Giants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Giants_(NL) \"New York Giants (NL)\") (now the [San Francisco Giants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco_Giants \"San Francisco Giants\")), who won the World Series five times. Both teams moved to California in 1958.[[500]](#cite_note-507) There is one [Minor League Baseball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minor_League_Baseball \"Minor League Baseball\") team in the city, the Mets-affiliated [Brooklyn Cyclones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brooklyn_Cyclones \"Brooklyn Cyclones\"),[[501]](#cite_note-508) and the city gained a club in the independent [Atlantic League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_League \"Atlantic League\") when the [Staten Island FerryHawks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Staten_Island_FerryHawks \"Staten Island FerryHawks\") began play in 2022.[[502]](#cite_note-509)\n\nThe city's National Basketball Association teams are the [New York Knicks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Knicks \"New York Knicks\"), who play at [Madison Square Garden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madison_Square_Garden \"Madison Square Garden\"), and the [Brooklyn Nets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brooklyn_Nets \"Brooklyn Nets\"), who play at the [Barclays Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barclays_Center \"Barclays Center\"). The [New York Liberty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Liberty \"New York Liberty\") is the city's [Women's National Basketball Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Women's_National_Basketball_Association \"Women's National Basketball Association\") team. The first national college-level basketball championship, the [National Invitation Tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Invitation_Tournament \"National Invitation Tournament\"), was held in New York in 1938 and remains in the city.[[503]](#cite_note-510)\n\nThe metropolitan area is home to three National Hockey League teams. The [New York Rangers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Rangers \"New York Rangers\"), one of the league's [Original Six](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Original_Six \"Original Six\"), play at Madison Square Garden in Manhattan. The [New York Islanders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Islanders \"New York Islanders\"), traditionally representing [Long Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long_Island \"Long Island\"), play in [UBS Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UBS_Arena \"UBS Arena\") in [Elmont, New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elmont,_New_York \"Elmont, New York\"), but played in Brooklyn's Barclays Center from 2015 to 2020. The [New Jersey Devils](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Jersey_Devils \"New Jersey Devils\") play at [Prudential Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prudential_Center \"Prudential Center\") in nearby [Newark, New Jersey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newark,_New_Jersey \"Newark, New Jersey\").\n\nNew York City is represented in Major League Soccer by [New York City FC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City_FC \"New York City FC\"), who play their home games at Yankee Stadium,[[504]](#cite_note-511) and the [New York Red Bulls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Red_Bulls \"New York Red Bulls\"), who play their home games at [Sports Illustrated Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sports_Illustrated_Stadium \"Sports Illustrated Stadium\") in nearby [Harrison, New Jersey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison,_New_Jersey \"Harrison, New Jersey\").[[505]](#cite_note-512) [Gotham FC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gotham_FC \"Gotham FC\") in the [National Women's Soccer League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Women's_Soccer_League \"National Women's Soccer League\") also plays their home games at Sports Illustrated Stadium and will relocate to [Etihad Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Etihad_Park \"Etihad Park\") in New York City in 2028.[[506]](#cite_note-513) [Brooklyn FC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brooklyn_FC_(2024) \"Brooklyn FC (2024)\") is a professional soccer club based in Brooklyn, fielding a women's team in the first division [USL Super League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USL_Super_League \"USL Super League\") starting in 2024 and a men's team in the second division [USL Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USL_Championship \"USL Championship\") in 2025.[[507]](#cite_note-shared-514) New York was a host city for the [FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA_World_Cup \"FIFA World Cup\") on two occasions, though all games were played in [East Rutherford, New Jersey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Rutherford,_New_Jersey \"East Rutherford, New Jersey\"). For the [1994 FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994_FIFA_World_Cup \"1994 FIFA World Cup\"), matches were played at [Giants Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giants_Stadium \"Giants Stadium\"), including one of the semi-final games.[[508]](#cite_note-515)[[509]](#cite_note-516) New York City was one of eleven US host cities for the [2026 FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_FIFA_World_Cup \"2026 FIFA World Cup\"), with multiple matches, including the [final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_FIFA_World_Cup_final \"2026 FIFA World Cup final\") played at MetLife Stadium.[[510]](#cite_note-517)[[511]](#cite_note-518)\n\nThe annual [US Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/US_Open_(tennis) \"US Open (tennis)\") is one of four [Grand Slam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Slam_(tennis) \"Grand Slam (tennis)\") tennis tournaments and is held at the [National Tennis Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USTA_National_Tennis_Center \"USTA National Tennis Center\") in [Flushing Meadows–Corona Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flushing_Meadows–Corona_Park \"Flushing Meadows–Corona Park\").[[512]](#cite_note-519) The [New York City Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City_Marathon \"New York City Marathon\"), which courses through all five boroughs, is the world's largest running marathon, with a world-record 59,226 finishers in 2025, who came from 132 nations.[[513]](#cite_note-520) The [Millrose Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Millrose_Games \"Millrose Games\") is an annual track and field meet held at the [Fort Washington Avenue Armory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Washington_Avenue_Armory \"Fort Washington Avenue Armory\"), whose featured event is the [Wanamaker Mile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wanamaker_Mile \"Wanamaker Mile\").[[514]](#cite_note-521) Boxing is a prominent part of the city's sporting scene, with events like the [New York Golden Gloves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Golden_Gloves
